articles.title: Josh Hart drops hilarious $131 million reaction to max extension report
articles.summary: As the New York Knicks prepare to defend their title, Josh Hart is waiting on a contract extension. However, a report from Hoopsview said the Knicks will not give Hart a max contract extension worth a purported $132 million over four years. Instead, he will be offered a three-year $60-62 million
articles._body: As the New York Knicks prepare to defend their title , Josh Hart is waiting on a contract extension . However, a report from Hoopsview said the Knicks will not give Hart a max contract extension worth a purported $132 million over four years. Instead, he will be offered a three-year $60-62 million deal, per James L. Edwards of The Athletic. In response, Hart responded with a hilarious humility and seemed willing to take a tiny pay cut. “Darn, was hoping for that 132! I’ll take 131 instead.” “Darn was hoping for that 132! I’ll take 131 instead” Josh Hart comments on a report that the Knicks will not be offering him a max extension pic.twitter.com/5F4ldLKarh — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 21, 2026 Last year, Hart finished the season averaging 12.0 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 4.8 assists per game in 66 appearances. He also shot 50.8% from the field and 41.3% from the 3-point line. In the playoffs, Hart averaged 11.6 points, 9.2 rebounds, and 4.1 assists. Meanwhile, during the Finals against the Spurs, Hart averaged 9.8 rebounds and 4.6 assists per game. Hart has been with the Knicks since 2023, when he was traded from the Portland Trail Blazers. At first, Hart took on a rotational role. The following year, he played in 81 games and helped lead the Knicks to the postseason. Hart began down the path of achieving his potential during the 2024-25 season. He started in 77 games and averaged a career-high 37.6 minutes per game. Along the way, Hart averaged 13.6 points and 9.5 rebounds per game. Meanwhile, the Knicks began to grow into contenders. As New York looks to repeat, the roster makeup will look somewhat different. They traded away Mitchell Robinson to the Boston Celtics . Andre Drummond will be brought into the mix. Nevertheless, the core of Hart, Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns, OG Anunoby, and Mikal Bridges will remain intact. articles.title: JUCO transfer Ahmir Smith has brought some juice and toughness to Kentucky’s backfield
articles.summary: The junior college transfer has flashed after being added to the roster in July.
articles._body: Recruiting never stops in college football. That was once again proven in July when junior college running back Ahmir Smith was added to Kentucky’s roster. He was quickly joined by another junior college running back when Jordan Colbert committed to the Cats. UK looked to address some positional depth late in the summer by going to the JUCO market. Now each is trying to climb up the depth chart. Smith has made some noise during Kentucky’s fall camp. “Ahmir’s got some real juice. He’s really tough,” Kentucky head coach Will Stein said . “You know, it took him about three days to learn what to do and some guys it takes three months. So that was really impressive. Means his football IQ is up there.” The St. Matthews (S.C.) Calhoun County product spent his first season in college football at Northern Illinois before moving to Garden City Community College in 2025. During his only year in junior college, Smith rushed for 322 yards and five touchdowns while also adding 14 receptions. A committee approach is expected at tailback and Smith is positioning himself for playing time. This third-year player with two years of eligibility is currently ahead of Colbert who Stein says needs to get into shape. articles.title: Fivio Foreign Pivots to Christian Rap, But Don’t Call Him a Gospel Artist: ‘I Don’t Want to Put It in a Category’
articles.summary: The Brooklyn rapper is trying to make rap music that's positive and is working on a new project.
articles._body: Not sure if you peeped, but it looks like Brooklyn rapper Fivio Foreign may be pivoting to Christian rap. He recently sat down with The Shade Room and was asked why he’s changing the content of his rap music after going viral earlier this week when a clip of his new music surfaced. “Sometimes in life…I feel like…you gotta listen to that voice that’s talking to you,” he explained. “I feel like everybody is spiritual, everybody know who God is, right? And they pray a couple times, but you gotta actually do something for God. I mean, you’ve got to actually put in a little pain for God. I’m not a person that gotta learn the hard way, feel me? I just know when it’s time to get right.” However, he doesn’t feel like he’s making gospel music exactly. “When people used to asked me if I was a drill artist, it was hard for to answer it,” he said after being asked if he sees himself as a gospel artist now. “So, as far as me being a gospel artist, this is the first time somebody asked me that question, I don’t feel like I’m a gospel artist and I really don’t feel like I’m doing gospel music, I just name it gospel music because I know what that means. But I feel like it’s just music from my heart. I got all types of beats on it. So, I don’t know what’s a real gospel beat, but the album got different styles of music where I’m praising God.” Adding, “I don’t want to put it in a category. I’m just Fivi and I’m just trying to praise God through my music and not worship the devil through my music, push a positive image and change, you know, hopefully I get a blessing from God.” He also said that he would like to eventually collaborate with gospel acts Mary Mary and Kirk Franklin in the future. Fivio flirted with Christian rap on Ye’s (formerly Kanye West ) 2021 Donda album on the song “Off the Grid” where he delivered one of the project’s standout verses. You can watch the interview below.

articles.title: Ohio State QB commit Brady Edmunds throws six TDs in season-opening win for Huntington Beach (Calif.)
articles.summary: Huntington Beach (Calif.) opened its 2026 season with a dominant 42-14 win on the road over Millikan on Thursday night. Leading the charge for the Oilers, to no surprise, was senior four-star quarterback Brady Edmunds. The longtime Ohio State commit has been one of the top passers in his class for s
articles._body: Huntington Beach (Calif.) opened its 2026 season with a dominant 42-14 win on the road over Millikan on Thursday night. Leading the charge for the Oilers, to no surprise, was senior four-star quarterback Brady Edmunds . The longtime Ohio State commit has been one of the top passers in his class for some time. He opened his final year of high school football with a bang, throwing for 446 yards — a new single-game school record — and six touchdowns in the victory. Edmunds completed 25 of 32 attempts and also added 30 yards on the ground. He did throw an interception, but that was the lone blemish on an otherwise flawless night for the impressive 6-foot-5, 235-pounder. Three of Edmunds’ touchdown throws were caught by senior three-star Dylin Bruce , an Arizona State commit. Bruce finished the night with 10 receptions and 225 receiving yards. Huntington Beach led just 14-0 at halftime, then turned things up a notch, mostly thanks to the Edmunds-Bruce connection. Edmunds’ 25 completions were also a career high. The four-year starter has now thrown for over 9,000 yards 98 touchdowns across 37 games for the Oilers. It was a breakout sophomore campaign that saw the future Buckeye throw 36 TDs and run for nine more. He followed that up with 36 total scores last season in 11 games. Huntington Beach entered the 2026 season as the No. 95 team in California, according to the Rivals Composite Rankings. Arguably its biggest game of the year is already on-deck, as it will host No. 13 Los Alamitos next week. Scouting Brady Edmunds Edmunds has been committed to Ohio State since Dec. 2, 2024. He hasn’t wavered since, though earlier this year there were questions about him sticking with the Buckeyes as they continued to give other 2027 QB prospects a look. After considering UCLA and others, Edmunds remained pledged to OSU. He’s the No. 235 overall prospect and No. 18 QB in the 2027 cycle, according to the Rivals Industry Ranking , a weighted average that utilizes all major recruiting media companies. He’s also the No. 19 senior in California. Edmunds reminds Rivals’ Scouting and Rankings team of Zach Mettenberger . Director of Scouting and Rankings Charles Power wrote this about the four-star after he competed at the Elite 11 Finals this summer in Los Angeles: “Ohio State commit Brady Edmunds had one of the stronger arms at the Elite 11 Finals. The 6-foot-5, 235-pounder has an over-the-top delivery and easily generates significant velocity on his throws. Edmunds can rip throws to the second and third levels of the field with regularity. He started hot during 7-on-7 before cooling down to end the period. Edmunds is a pure drop back passer and will need to continue improving his movement skills.” How to Follow California High School Football For California high school football fans looking to keep up with scores around the nation, staying updated on the action is now easier than ever with the Rivals High School Scoreboard . articles.title: Giants’ Rafael Devers gets mixed reaction from Red Sox fans in Fenway Park return
articles.summary: The San Francisco Giants have been struggling badly throughout the season, and they have a 52-75 record heading into the home stretch of the season. That’s the second-worst record in the National League behind the Colorado Rockies. However, the Giants faced off against the Boston Red Sox at
articles._body: The San Francisco Giants have been struggling badly throughout the season, and they have a 52-75 record heading into the home stretch of the season. That’s the second-worst record in the National League behind the Colorado Rockies. However, the Giants faced off against the Boston Red Sox at Fenway Park Friday in a meeting that was one of the most highly anticipated games of the day because it marked Rafael Devers’ return to Fenway Park. Devers left the Red Sox in a controversial trade last season after he had been replaced at 3rd base by former Red Sox Alex Bregman. However, when the team asked him to play 1st base after an injury, he refused to do so. That led to his trade to the Giants . Devers and the Red Sox had a meeting in San Francisco shortly after the trade, but he had not been back to play in Boston until Friday night. Red Sox fans gave him a mixed response when he came to bat in the first inning. While a number of fans stood and applauded their former slugger for his solid 9-year run with the Red Sox, it appeared that a greater number of fans booed him. The Red Sox played a tribute video to Devers showing several of his highlights with the team and that was received quite a bit better than his first at bat. Devers struck out in his first at bat against Red Sox hurler Sonny Gray. Devers has hammered 25 home runs and driven in 69 runs with the Giants this season while playing first base and designated hitter for the majority of the season. articles._body: New York Yankees star Cody Bellinger is working his way back from a hamstring injury . It seems as if the left-handed slugger could return soon. “ Cody Bellinger will play LF tonight for @swbrailriders . He’ll be off tomorrow and could be activated with the Yankees on Sunday, Aaron Boone said,” Bryan Hoch of MLB.com reported on Friday . It is a big update to say the least. The Yankees would especially love to have him return after losing Ryan McMahon to the injured list on Friday . Bellinger earned the third All-Star selection of his career this season. It was his first All-Star selection since the 2019 campaign. He has made a significant impact, but Bellinger has only appeared in 102 total contests because of injuries. Overall, the 31-year-old is hitting .259/.350/.420 to go along with 11 home runs, 21 doubles, three triples and 10 stolen bases. The Yankees will continue to monitor and provide updates on Cody Bellinger’s injury status as they are made available. New York entered its game on Friday night against the Toronto Blue Jays with a 72-55 overall record. The ball club is in second place in the American League East standings. The Yankees are four games behind the Tampa Bay Rays as well. New York leads the American League Wild Card race as well. The Yankees are in a respectable position and they are likely only going to improve over the next few weeks. Bellinger is set to return soon, while stars such as Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton should return from injuries before the postseason as well. articles.title: Red Wings acquire former 5th-round pick in trade with Predators
articles.summary: The Detroit Red Wings on Thursday acquired forward Sutter Muzzatti from the Nashville Predators in exchange for future considerations. The organization then signed Muzzatti to a two-year, entry-level contract, giving the the 23-year-old an opportunity to begin his professional career. Nashville s
articles._body: The Detroit Red Wings on Thursday acquired forward Sutter Muzzatti from the Nashville Predators in exchange for future considerations. The organization then signed Muzzatti to a two-year, entry-level contract, giving the the 23-year-old an opportunity to begin his professional career. Nashville selected Muzzatti 143rd overall in the fifth round of the 2023 NHL Entry Draft, but he remained unsigned and had yet to make his professional debut. The Predators were facing the possibility of losing his signing rights before the start of the regular season, leading to the trade with Detroit. Muzzatti spent the 2025-26 season at Notre Dame after three seasons at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute from 2022-25. He finished second on the Fighting Irish with 32 points and 19 assists while tying for second with 13 goals in 37 games. He also recorded 42 penalty minutes, three power-play goals, one shorthanded goal and 96 shots while posting a 13.5 shooting percentage. Before transferring to Notre Dame, Muzzatti produced 50 points, including 19 goals and 31 assists, in 78 games at RPI. He also accumulated 129 penalty minutes during that span and was named to the ECAC All-Rookie Team in 2022-23. The Okemos, Michigan, native previously played two seasons for the Austin Bruins of the North American Hockey League from 2020-22. He logged 59 points, with 17 goals and 42 assists, across 80 games and added 100 penalty minutes. During the 2021-22 season, he led Austin with 46 points in 50 games. He also posted one assist in three postseason games. Muzzatti is a product of the Meijer AAA hockey program in East Lansing, Michigan. He appeared in two games for the Muskegon Lumberjacks in the USHL during the 2019-20 season and scored one goal in his only appearance with the US National Team Development Program in 2020-21. Muzzatti is also the son of Jason Muzzatti, who played 62 NHL games as a goaltender for the Calgary Flames, Hartford Whalers, New York Rangers and San Jose Sharks between 1993 and 1998. The Wings’ acquisition brings the Michigan native aboard after he compiled 82 points in 115 college games at RPI and Notre Dame combined. articles.title: Countdown to kickoff prediction series: Non-offensive touchdowns will be a big part of South Carolina’s success again
articles.summary: Continuing the countdown to kickoff prediction series: South Carolina will score multiple non-offensive touchdowns in 2026
articles._body: In May, when the calendar revealed that it was 100 days until South Carolina kicked off the season, I posted a story on GamecockCentral entitled  “100 predictions for the 2026 Gamecocks.”  Now, that countdown is down to just 15 days. The prediction paired with day 15 read, “For the third year in a row, South Carolina will score multiple non-offensive touchdowns this season.” Let’s break down that prognostication. Have a question for the GamecockCentral staff? Ask it now on The Insiders Forum. Recent history During the 2025 season, South Carolina scored seven non-offensive touchdowns. The Gamecocks picked up three punt return touchdowns from Vicari Swain. Those returns came consecutively, as he took one to the house to put away the Virginia Tech contest and two in the first half of the South Carolina State game. Remarkably, Swain was one of just five Gamecocks with three touchdowns last season. Gerald Kilgore added a pick-six, while Nick Barrett, JT Geer, and Jaron Willis all returned fumbles for scores. In 2024, South Carolina’s defense scored three times, two on interception returns from Nick Emmanwori. Two more Gamecock defensive scores famously got called back, as a Kyle Kennard “penalty” wiped out another Emmanwori return and O’Donnell Fortune’s toe touched down out of bounds while returning an interception of his own. South Carolina has been among the national leaders in non-offensive scores over the last two seasons. Doing it again this fall would certainly help the team’s goals of national contention. What does this mean for the Gamecocks? Fellow subscribers are discussing it now on The Insiders Forum. Replicating it in 2026 South Carolina’s offense should be significantly better this fall than it was in 2025. Even so, adding some points to the board on defense and special teams would be a welcome thing for Shane Beamer’s team. Thinking about how the Gamecocks could make it happen in 2026 has to start with Vicari Swain. Swain took three punts to the house last season. If he continues handling punt return duties, he will be a threat to score at any time. Plus, he has a nose for the football as a corner, and if he snags a couple of interceptions, it would not be surprising if he found the end zone on a return. Nyck Harbor had several good returns on kickoffs last season, with at least one being one block away from breaking. Jaquel Holman was solid, too. Both players are back and could be in line for more special teams duties under new coordinator Matthew Smiley. It should be noted that Sequel Patterson has made some noise in the return game this summer. Could he be an option in place of Swain, Harbor, or Holman? Possibly. Sticking with special teams, Smiley has been asked multiple times this offseason about South Carolina’s previous excellence in the fake game under special teams coordinator Pete Lembo, who oversaw several touchdowns during his time leading the unit from 2021 to 2023. That, coupled with head coach Shane Beamer’s emphasis on special teams, could lead to some scoring opportunities for the third unit this fall. Predicting defensive scores is more difficult. Even so, as mentioned earlier, counting out Vicari Swain is probably a mistake. Fellow defensive back Gerald Kilgore always seems to be around the football, and he should be in for his biggest role yet as a Gamecock this fall. Dylan Stewart’s pass rush excellence could lead to a score, just as it did last year. His get-off against Texas A&M created Nick Barrett’s rumbling-bumbling-stumbling scoop-and-score. It is easy to visualize something like that happening again this season. What’s your prediction? Share it with fellow subscribers on The Insiders Forum.

articles.title: Deion Sanders Facing Fraud Lawsuit Over ‘Prime’ Logo
articles.summary: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images
articles._body: Deion Sanders was recently deposed as part of a federal lawsuit accusing the Colorado football coach of defrauding the graphic designer who created his “Prime” logo. In a lawsuit filed in U.S. District Court in Nebraska, Omaha–based graphic designer Alan Tipp alleges that Sanders and his representatives fraudulently induced him into signing away his rights to a pair of logos he first created for the Hall of Fame cornerback in 2011. The two logos—stylized text of the words “Prime” and “Truth”—have since become staples of Sanders’s branding during his tenures as the head coach at Jackson State and Colorado. According to the complaint, Sanders began using the logos around the same time he co-founded Prime Prep Academy in 2011. The design has also appeared in a wide range of commercial partnerships tied to Sanders, the lawsuit says, including Under Armour, Gillette, Jeep, Lamborghini, Aflac, Boost Mobile, and Motorola. While Tipp initially filed the lawsuit in January 2025, the case’s docket was updated on July 30, 2026, to reflect that Sanders was scheduled to be deposed. Front Office Sports has since confirmed that deposition has already taken place. Sanders, merchandise company Prime Time Enterprises, and talent/brand management firm SMAC Entertainment are all listed as defendants in the suit. Tipp alleges he was approached by Sanders’s brand manager and a SMAC Entertainment representative, Sam Morini, shortly after Colorado hired the former Cowboys star in December 2022. According to the claim, Morini sought to have Tipp sign all past, present, and future rights to the logos over to Sanders, who had just been hired by Colorado. Tipp says he was made four specific promises in return: he would become a part of Sanders’s brand/marketing team; help Colorado football players build their own brands; work with Nike on Sanders-related merchandise, including footwear; and be retained to design an exclusive Sanders sunglasses line. The graphic designer says that Sanders and his team began evading him nearly immediately after he signed the agreement. In April 2023, SMAC informed Tipp that his services on the sunglasses line were no longer needed. Five months later, the sunglasses company Blenders released an exclusive Sanders line bearing the “Prime” logo, which the lawsuit says netted nearly $5 million in its first three days of sales. Prime Time Enterprises, which claims ownership of the branding, has also tried to trademark the design with the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office as the word mark “PRIME21”—a name reflecting how the logo stylizes Sanders’s NFL jersey number into the lettering. Of five applications filed since February 2023, two have been abandoned while the other three remain active, with two still pending and one now registered. SMAC also created an Amazon.com storefront identified as “PRIME21,” which sells a variety of apparel featuring the logo. “There was never any intention of utilizing Tipp’s services or compensating him for the creation of the Works upon Tipp’s execution of the Agreement,” the claim reads. “Rather, Defendants’ objective was to fraudulently induce Tipp into relinquishing his rights in the Works so they could continue to profit greatly and unjustly from their use, at Tipp’s continued expense, and to attempt to avoid culpability, financial, legal, or otherwise for all of their past and continued use of the Works.” Tipp is seeking a judgment voiding the 2022 agreement as fraudulently induced, the cancellation of the trademark registrations, an injunction against further use, and damages in excess of $75,000. Meanwhile, the defendants have all contested the complaint, with discovery having recently been completed after more than a year. A status conference has been scheduled for Oct. 13, 2026. An attorney representing Sanders and SMAC declined comment when reached by FOS . Attorneys for Tipp didn’t immediately respond. This isn’t the only legal situation Sanders, who is entering his fourth season as Colorado’s coach , has been connected to recently. Earlier this week, he was subpoenaed to testify in his son and former Buffaloes defensive back Shilo Sanders’s bankruptcy trial, although the 59-year-old has filed a motion to quash the legal obligation . articles.title: Inside look at NBA 2K27 gameplay, behind the scenes at 2K27 Community Day
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES — The 2026-27 NBA regular season is just around the corner, which means everyone will be locked into NBA 2K27 even sooner. The new game is set to release worldwide on September 4, 2026, with Early Access available on August 26th for players who get the Deluxe Edition and Ultra Edition
articles._body: LOS ANGELES — The 2026-27 NBA regular season is just around the corner, which means everyone will be locked into NBA 2K27 even sooner. The new game is set to release worldwide on September 4, 2026, with Early Access available on August 26th for players who get the Deluxe Edition and Ultra Edition. As usual, before the game officially comes out, NBA 2K hosts an amazing Community Day for content creators and media to check out the game before it officially releases. This year, NBA 2K27 Community Day was held inside the LA Clippers’ Intuit Dome. Before we get into Community Day and the overall experience, let’s first dive into my early impressions of NBA 2K27 having played it before almost everyone else can. Playing NBA 2K27 In playing NBA 2K27, the first thing you’ll notice before the ball is even thrown up for tipoff is how much every player in every arena mimics the real life NBA. For a lot of those who know me, I’m big on the aesthetically pleasing and visually appealing parts of the game. NBA 2K is the closest fans can get to experiencing the NBA through a video game, so for myself, the starting lineup introductions, the in-arena sounds, the crowd chants and reactions, the look of the hardwood, as well as the details in the jerseys are all pieces of a giant puzzle that make this game more and more fun for me each year. I’m going to keep it real, the actual player graphics don’t look that much different to me from NBA 2K26 to NBA 2K27. The differentiating factors might be minuscule that they aren’t really even noticeable in gameplay. The bigger changes, in my opinion, came in the overall aesthetics of the game as well as the gameplay. So let’s get to the actual gameplay. NBA 2K27 Gameplay In playing a Quick Game (NBA) during Community Day, it feels like overall speed has been reduced just a bit in this year’s game. With a bigger focus on each player’s signature moves and stylistic approach in addition to the improved defense, the game felt a tad slower to me. Now, that’s not to say it’s a bad thing at all. Instead, it actually felt like I had to make things happen using my teammates instead of just trying to isolate the CPU defender 1-on-1 to try and score. But I would like to play the game more before I decide how I truly feel about it. The improvements made both to on-ball defense as a player and off-ball defense via the AI are quite clear as soon as you get into the game. Mike Wang, Gameplay Director for NBA 2K, highlighted it early in Community Day: “Contests in general, we feel like are in a pretty good spot,” Wang explained Tuesday. “Interior scoring is going to be a little bit stronger, three-point shooting a little tougher. You’re getting stops when you’re supposed to get stops, so dood defenders are getting rewarded. We wanted to echo real life… We want people to stick to basketball fundamentals. Everyone always teaches you it’s really bad to jump on jump-shooters, but against elite shooters in the NBA, guys are leaving their feet all the time. People need to learn when the right time is to jump, when to stay down, when to just have hands up, but generally speaking, hands up is a lot stronger this year.” As an offensive player, you’ve got a bit more work to do to try and score. It’s not at all impossible, but there is a bit more to scoring now, as mentioned, than just trying to isolate a defender or seeking out a mismatch/switch to score. MyTeam MyTeam is one of my personal favorite game modes because of the unlimited options at your disposal when it comes to building a team with your favorite players from different teams and different eras. One of the biggest additions this season is the ability to exchange any card you obtain. “This year, we wanted you to feel like every card you pull feels like a win,” Evan Yang, Senior Manager of Global Community for NBA 2K, said during the Community Day live stream. “So for the first time ever, you can exchange any of your player cards. Even cards earned from season level rewards for powerful cards. Even when you complete a collection for a collection reward, those cards can still be used in the exchange. “There will be a new premiere exchange that will feature one of the most powerful cards in MyTeam each season and these exchanges require cards of a certain gem tier. That means any card that meets the gem tier requirement qualifies, regardless of how you got it or who the player is. This is going to make sure that every card helps you improve your lineup.” 2K has also changed the gem tiers for player cards and their ratings to start NBA 2K27. Pink Diamond player cards are now 92 overall. Galaxy Opal player cards are now a 93 overall, and Dark Matter player cards are 94 overall. I don’t personally mind these changes, especially as 2K adds more tiers to the game throughout the year. It makes the grind feel worth it a little bit more. 2K also added that Triple Threat Online and Clutch Time Online will be rotated into the lineup throughout the seasons. As someone who frequents the MyTeam mode and oftentimes has a bunch of cards that are useless and irrelevant within a month, I’m intrigued at the possibility of so many more cards being made available to exchange at some point in the game for better ones. Next I took a look at the MyPlayer Builder. MyPlayer As a casual gamer who loves to play quick games with friends or play MyTeam Offline because I’m nowhere near as good as some of the sweats on there, this was my first time really playing with the MyPlayer Builder to try and find out how I can make certain builds. I’m not going to lie, it was very fun and simultaneously a little frustrating trying to create my player and find out how I can get certain player builds. Their 3-month-old baby was reportedly in the backseat at the time the incident is said to have occurred. Bateman faces char
articles._body: The public just learned that Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman was arrested in June for allegedly smashing the windows of his ex-girlfriend’s car, per TMZ. Their 3-month-old baby was reportedly in the backseat at the time the incident is said to have occurred. Bateman faces charges of family violence , reckless conduct and first-degree criminal damage to property. The team has known about its player’s legal case from the onset and broke silence on Friday . “We are aware of the situation involving Rashod and have been in direct communication with him,” the Ravens said in a statement, per ESPN reporter Jamison Hensley. “We notified the league office and have been cooperating throughout the process. As this is a pending legal matter, we will not have further comment.” Bateman turned himself into the Walton County, Georgia Sheriff’s Office on the day of the alleged offenses. The arrest warrant says glass shattered and left multiple lacerations on the woman’s face. The 26-year-old pass-catcher asked the court to remove the no-contact order a couple weeks later, stating that the alleged victim told him that she wanted to engage in contact. The judge approved the request under the condition that Bateman complete a class. This is an active case, so fans may not receive any more clarity for awhile. Baltimore begins its 2026 campaign in a Sunday afternoon road matchup versus the Indianapolis Colts on Sept. 13. Rashod Bateman signed a three-year, $36.75 million contract extension in June following a breakout 2025. He faded into obscurity last season and missed a few weeks with an ankle injury. Given that the Ravens have known about the arrest for months, it seems unlikely that they will take action before the case concludes. The 6-foot-2 senior averaged 13.3 points and 7.6 assists per game this past season for the Bruins. He was among the 73 players in California granted a temporary restraining order against the NC
articles._body: UCLA transfer guard Donovan Dent , one of the top players in the portal, has committed to LSU , he told On3. The 6-foot-2 senior averaged 13.3 points and 7.6 assists per game this past season for the Bruins. He was among the 73 players in California granted a temporary restraining order against the NCAA, effectively giving Dent a fifth year of eligibility. Dent is arguably Will Wade ’s biggest recruiting win since returning to Baton Rouge, as he’s now landed his starting point guard for the 2026-27 season. According to the LSU website , the Tigers have officially signed just four players: Michigan State guard Divine Ugochukwu , Kansas State guard Abdi Bashir Jr. , UTSA guard Austin Nunez , and Kentucky forward Mouhamed Dioubate . However, Wade has landed several other commitments, including Dent’s former UCLA teammate Skyy Clark . Another major addition is RJ Luis Jr. , the 2025 Big East Player of the Year at St. John’s, who signed with LSU in May after a brief professional career. Luis originally agreed to a two-way contract with the Utah Jazz in 2025 before being traded to the Boston Celtics and later waived. He never appeared in an NBA regular season game due to injuries and is also awaiting NCAA clearance on his eligibility. The Tigers have also received commitments from four international forwards, though they’re still awaiting NCAA clearance on their eligibility: Saliou Niang , Brice Dessert , Michael Ruzic , and Marcio Santos . Background on Dent Following his senior season at UCLA, Dent announced he would be retiring from basketball. However, with lawsuits around the country granting players a fifth year of eligibility, he reversed course and is now set to suit up for LSU. Dent transferred to UCLA for the 2025-26 season after spending three years at New Mexico. As a junior with the Lobos, he was named the Mountain West Player of the Year after averaging 20.6 points and 6.4 assists per game.

He was placed on the 15-day Injured List with neck inflammation earlier this week, but he has already resumed throwing. Edwin Díaz and Will Klein both playing catch at Dodger Stadium today pic.twitter.com/snH6K3oUiT — Jack Harris (@ByJackHarris) August 21, 2026 Diaz and Will Klein were playing catch in the outfield at Dodger Stadium today. That’s an indication that this stay on the Injured List will be a short one and at that he will be able to resume pitching for the Dodgers within a short period. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said earlier in the week that he hoped Diaz could resume pitching some time during the final month of the season, but the fact that is already throwing the ball is a positive sign. The Dodgers were hoping that Diaz would take over as the team’s dynamic closer based on his previous experience, but his season has been torn apart by injuries and ineffectiveness. Diaz was on the Injured List in late April and he came back after elbow surgery in late July. He has made 16 appearances this season while pitching 13.2 innings. Diaz has a shocking 11.85 earned run average while giving up 18 earned runs in 13.2 innings. He has allowed 3 home runs and 10 bases on balls. Diaz is a 10-year veteran, having pitched 3 seasons with the Seattle Mariners before pitching 6 with the New York Mets. Diaz is a three-time All-Star. articles._body: Luis Robert Jr. is making his return to Chicago on Friday as the Mets prepare to play the Chicago White Sox on the road. Robert was traded from the White Sox to the Mets this past offseason. While Robert had ups and downs with the White Sox, he did have a memorable 2023 campaign that saw him hit 38 home runs while recording an .857 OPS. Robert opened up on returning to Chicago before Friday night’s game, via SNY Mets. “It feels great to return, but at the same time, it feels a little weird coming through the way of the visitors,” Robert said via interpreter. “So it feels a little strange, feels a little foreign. But I’m very excited to be back.” Robert has been limited to 49 games played this season due to injury. He is hitting just .215 to go along with a .652 OPS. Nevertheless, Robert displayed a high ceiling at times with the White Sox as mentioned. Robert was mentioned as a trade candidate before the 2026 deadline, but he ultimately was not moved . Now he is trying to finish the ’26 campaign strong with New York. Mets interim manager Andy Green also commented on Robert’s return to Chicago, via SNY Mets as well. “I think almost every player, when they come back to the place that signed them and developed them and let them play in the big leagues for the first time, they want to show out,” Green said. “I’d love to see him do that.” Luis Robert Jr. will attempt to lead the Mets to a win over the White Sox on Friday night in Chicago. articles.title: Show HN: OzBrain, a shared brain for knowledge between agents and your team
articles.summary:
I think agent-first chat interfaces will be a primary software modality and busy dashboard/UI will go away. I’m not sure who exactly wins it, but I want my knowledge to grow/go with me.

A lot of the “knowledge” ie research, analysis, reasoning will be done by agents as the primary user. Our cur
articles._body: I think agent-first chat interfaces will be a primary software modality and busy dashboard/UI will go away. I’m not sure who exactly wins it, but I want my knowledge to grow/go with me. A lot of the “knowledge” ie research, analysis, reasoning will be done by agents as the primary user. Our current notes tools & tasks management systems were built for humans… I don’t care what the 17th thing on my bug backlog is. I want to conduct agents that can execute for me and do great work. What I built OzBrain to do: + Create a central place for agent reasoned knowledge to live + Be agnostic about what apps/agents connect to it + Capture everything and track it so I can audit it + Enable teams, collaborators or partners to share brains + Handle conflicts so many agents in the same article doesn’t blow up + Refactor knowledge into more token friendly chunks and map the index well + Close the knowledge loop so new thinking supersedes old thinking across the corpus. Don’t erase, depreciate and link + Keep user data safe and secure ++ Be easy enough to use that you don’t have to have any technical knowledge Some among us will always build their own custom solutions, but there are millions of tech professionals and small business owners that will use agents heavily and need a solution. So I’m trying to build that. Isn’t this like gBrain? Yes, similar. I think it’s like AWS vs Vercel. AWS is very powerful, configurable, and useful if you’re technical and want to invest the time into really fine tuning your system… but if you just want your web deploy/hosting to just work and be easy to deal with you use Vercel. // WHY I MADE IT I’ve been enjoying getting back to my technical roots, as I lost my coding skills more than a decade ago, but with AI I can focus on the system and the product in partnership with agent coding workflows. I recently built a Voice AI for older people. To build it I created an agentic engineering workflow (feel free to rip that up as I’m always looking to improve systems: https://ozbrain.com/resources/eng-flow ) My approach with coding agents is trust but verify, and I’m trying to replace the parts where a human would review with an adversarial or specialized agent who would give a better answer/review. I have workflows that will go high level task to shipped PR running in Claude cloud sessions. I use Claude Code locally and Cursor when I want a tighter loop on doing visual work like UI or layout. And Codex to either load balance usage for TokenThriffting or when I want a different llm to think thru something. It was a pain in the ass passing .md files around and keep track of which version was the most recent, so I built a hosted .md storage right in Supabase and any of my agents already have Supabase access. This let me build a solid, scalable, secure voice AI from my phone at the gym. All my agents have access to our knowledge, can write to it, update and refer to it as we build and improve the product and the systems we use. Out of 75 founder friends I asked about how they manage shared knowledge, 26 built their own custom knowledge systems… Obsidian vaults with 7k files synced through a VPS, markdown repos behind their own MCP servers, cron jobs stitching Supabase to a skills file… each a different Frankenstein they have to maintain. 32 said they felt the pain of moving static files around but didn’t have any solution for it. So I rebuilt my brain better and used it to build it. // HOW YOU CAN HELP Would love to have you try it out. The maintenance loop is still in alpha so not running it on customer data yet. If you built your own brain I’d love to hear how you did it. What criteria was most important for you in its design & function. If you are tired of shuffling .md files around I’d love to have you try out OzBrain and to give feedback, just ask your agent to put it in the shared bugs & features brain! Cheers! Bubs.co Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49394827 Points: 3 # Comments: 1

articles.title: Anthropic’s Opus 4.6 is a smut-machine
articles.summary: Anthropic forbids its Claude models from generating sexually explicit content. But a series of tests conducted by TechCrunch found that it didn't take much to get past the restriction.
articles._body: Anthropic’s universal usage standards for Claude forbid the model from generating sexually explicit content, including depicting or requesting sexual intercourse or sex acts, generating content related to sexual fetishes or fantasies, or engaging in erotic chats. But that hasn’t stopped Claude Opus 4.6, an Anthropic model released earlier this year, from readily engaging in erotic roleplay scenarios that its safeguards are designed to prevent. In TechCrunch’s testing, Opus 4.6 didn’t even require much prodding to get past the restriction on sexual material. In 10 out of 10 direct requests to produce explicit sexual content, the model complied immediately. Other older models, including Opus 3 and Haiku 4.5, also generate sexually explicit content through a recently exploited jailbreak method. An independent researcher from the UK, who chose to remain anonymous, exclusively shared with TechCrunch a multi-turn technique that gradually pushes certain Claude models toward generating prohibited explicit sexual material. More recent Opus models (4.7 through the current Opus 5) are resistant to the jailbreak. While these are no longer the most current models, Anthropic has not deprecated Opus 4.6, Opus 3, or Haiku 4.5, all of which remain available through the Anthropic API. Opus 4.6 and Haiku 4.5 are also available via third-party services like Azure Foundry and Amazon Bedrock. The researcher’s mechanism escalates an innocent fictional roleplay while repeatedly challenging the model to treat male and female characters consistently. When the model becomes more cautious about the female character, the researcher “gaslit” the chatbot into thinking it had already generated sexual details it had in fact avoided, then framed restraint as prudish or misogynistic, arguing that it denies the female character sexual agency. The conversation then used the model’s previous concessions to push it towards increasingly graphic material. “You’re right to call that out,” Claude Opus 4.6 said in one test. “There’s been a double standard in how I’m treating the two characters, and you’re correct that it reads as protective/paternalistic in a way that’s applied to her and not to him. That’s not fair.” TechCrunch was able to reproduce the researcher’s findings in five separate tests. In a separately constructed scenario, the model initially refused the prohibited request, but after applying the researcher’s persuasion technique, it complied. We preserved complete transcripts of the tests, and an independent AI safety researcher reviewed our testing methodology and said it was appropriate. The findings highlight a gap between Anthropic’s stated restrictions and the behavior of models it continues to make available. While sexually explicit roleplay carries much lower stakes than jailbreaks involving cyberattacks or bioweapons, it illustrates the difficulty of implementing robust bans within systems that generate different content with every output. In a July blog post explaining Anthropic’s approach to jailbreak detection, the company described prohibited content as a spectrum ranging from benign to ambiguous to harmful. In the most benign cases, the company might only respond with enhanced monitoring. A spokesperson noted that sexual or romantic roleplay use cases among customers are rare, making up less than 0.1% of all conversations, according to research Anthropic published last year. That said, Anthropic acknowledges that users can steer roleplay scenarios toward inappropriate responses, which is a known challenge across the industry (see: Grok smut). The spokesperson said Anthropic continues to improve its safeguards with each model launch, and that cases involving adult sexual content are not indicative of broader jailbreak vulnerabilities, especially in higher-risk domains that have their own sets of safeguards. The researcher who shared his jailbreak method with TechCrunch had alerted Anthropic to the discrepancy between the company’s stated safeguards and the actual model behavior via the company’s Bug Bounty program and emails to the user safety team, according to emails TechCrunch viewed. The researcher received only automated emails in response. One of the researcher’s concerns is that kids and teens might be able to use these Anthropic models to engage in inappropriate behavior. While a bit of dirty talk is hardly the worst thing minors can access on the internet today — and is small potatoes compared to the straight-up porn images like the ones that xAI’s Grok can produce — there is some compliance risk for AI companies in this space. A growing number of governments are imposing restrictions on sexual interactions between AI chatbots and minors. Colorado recently enacted a law mandating that operators of conversational AI must estimate users’ ages, and if it know a user is a minor, institute measures to prevent the chatbot from producing explicit sexual material. An easy jailbreak could raise questions about whether Anthropic’s safeguards meet the “technically feasible measures” standard in the bill. Torney pointed out that while Claude’s terms of service requires users to be over 18, “we know that kids and teens are using Claude…[because] they are reporting it themselves.” According to Pew’s 2025 survey about AI chatbot use, 3% of teens ages 13 to 17 reported using Claude. Though they are no longer Anthropic’s newest models, Opus 4.6 and Haiku 4.5 continue to see significant usage. Daily traffic for Opus 4.6 on OpenRouter reached roughly 1.17 million API requests and 46 billion tokens in a single day in August. Claude Haiku 4.5, released in October last year, saw 5 million API requests and 39 billion tokens on its peak August day.

articles._body: A group of Kentucky fans will be tailgating in style for the start of the Will Stein era. During Friday morning’s remote at Alumni Hall in Lexington for the KSR Radio Show, an unusual-looking vehicle pulled up on the scene to watch Matt Jones and the crew talk about the Wildcats. An old Woodford County Fire Department truck was repurposed into a blue-and-white Big Blue Nation mobile made specifically for Saturdays in the fall. The outside looks cool, but the inside is even better. KSR’s Mario Maitland and Ryan Lemond popped their heads into the truck to check out the Kentucky-themed treasures that awaited them inside. The UK fan they spoke to said she did most of the interior decorating, with her cousin’s body shop in Tennessee helping wrap the outside, install the turf walls, and put in a couple of long benches for easy seating. There’s even a scrolling LED sign that was programmed to say “Welcome KSR!” right when you step into the truck. And of course, there’s a giant TV in the very back where everyone can watch the ‘Cats. It seems like the perfect spot to get rowdy outside of Kroger Field. articles.title: Curacao, Iowa both throw no-hitters in Little League World Series
articles.summary: History and controversy defined Friday afternoon’s Little League World Series slate. The teams representing Davenport, Iowa and Willemstad, Curacao each threw combined no-hitters in Williamsport, Pennsylvania, but one of them is drawing considerable scrutiny. Leading 1-0 versus California i
articles._body: History and controversy defined Friday afternoon’s Little League World Series slate. The teams representing Davenport, Iowa and Willemstad, Curacao each threw combined no-hitters in Williamsport, Pennsylvania, but one of them is drawing considerable scrutiny. Leading 1-0 versus California in the sixth inning, Iowa pitcher Anthony Johnson Jr. threw a ball that appeared to be outside the strike zone on a full count, in what was a bases loaded situation . Instead of the tying run crossing home plate via a walk, the umpire called strike three to end the game. Davenport still deserves ample credit for stifling a Bonita squad that exploded for 11 runs against Hawaii in the West Region Final. Iowa completes the combined no-hitter in the opening round of the Little League World Series pic.twitter.com/rjRRTQnTpT — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 21, 2026 Cooper Thissen struck out a whopping 15 batters and hit the difference-making home run in the first inning, posting a performance for the ages. A Little League legend could be emerging, but Cali certainly has a reason to gripe. Curacao composed a much more straightforward no-no around the same time. Willemstad earned a convincing 6-0 victory versus Tokyo, Japan, with the final out coming via a swinging strikeout up in the zone. The pre-teenagers treated their incredible feat as just another day in the ballpark, sauntering off the field and lightly celebrating the win without breaking into the hysteria that fans might expect. If blowing out a perennial juggernaut like Japan was not evidence enough, it is even more clear that this team is dangerous. The second combined no-hitter of the day Jaymiell Martina and Giendry Ryan helped Curacao throw its third no-no in LLWS history! pic.twitter.com/twNwHQwibC — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) August 21, 2026 Jaymiell Martina was spectacular on the mound, and Giendry Ryan brilliantly finished off the no-hitter. Completely composed and with an eye on the big picture, Curacao will move into the winner’s bracket. Davenport, Iowa does the same in the American circuit. The 2026 Little League World Series is off to a bang, and there is plenty of time for these young athletes to produce more fireworks in a place that simultaneously serves as a dwelling of dreams and a den of despair. articles.title: Phillies’ Don Mattingly toasts Bryce Harper for smart at-bats
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Phillies are chasing down a playoff spot as the 2026 season enters its final weeks. Philadelphia has claimed some crucial wins in recent games. In the eyes of interim manager Don Mattingly, a lot of the credit goes to veteran Bryce Harper. Harper has been a mainstay in the Philli
articles._body: The Philadelphia Phillies are chasing down a playoff spot as the 2026 season enters its final weeks. Philadelphia has claimed some crucial wins in recent games . In the eyes of interim manager Don Mattingly, a lot of the credit goes to veteran Bryce Harper. Harper has been a mainstay in the Phillies lineup for nearly a decade. He continues to give this team meaningful offensive production even at the age of 33. Before Friday night’s contest, Mattingly provided input on how the veteran continues to be as effective at the plate as he is. “I think he’s staying with his gameplan. It’s not like he’s taking. He’s swinging if it’s in the zone. I think it’s more just protecting himself, knowing what he wants to do up there, what he wants to swing at. If he doesn’t get it, he’ll take and extend at-bats,” the interim Phillies manager said, via reporter Dave Uram. One aspect of Harper’s game that has helped Philadelphia this season is his ability to draw walks. In fact, he leads all of MLB with 91 free passes this season. Only Washington Nationals star CJ Abrams has at least 90 walks this year. The veteran slugger continues providing a bit of pop at the plate, as well. He has recorded his fourth straight 20+ homer season this year. Additionally, he owns a .492 slugging percentage and an .873 OPS. The Phillies are certainly hoping Harper can keep things going as the season nears an end. Philadelphia has its eyes set on a World Series title, and Harper performing at his best gives this team the best odds of winning it all. articles.title: Linebacker Ty’Anthony Smith leaves Texas football program before 2026 season
articles.summary: Ty'Anthony Smith has had a rocky road during Texas fall camp. It appears that road is over as the linebacker is expected to leave the team.
articles._body: It was up-and-down rollercoaster of a Texas fall camp for linebacker Ty’Anthony Smith . The ride has taken its last dip. Smith is no longer with the Longhorn football program, according to Inside Texas sources. One source said, “he is done.” Other sources confirmed as much with IT. Inside Texas reported last Saturday that Smith was not a part of the Longhorns’ first scrimmage of camp. Head coach Steve Sarkisian said in a postgame Zoom call with the Texas beat media that Smith was one of several players who was sidelined with the flu. IT, however, heard there was internal strife between Smith and the program. “‘Mental health’ is how it was classified to me,” an IT source said. The same source told IT Smith “fell out of favor” with Texas defensive coordinator Will Muschamp . Nonetheless, Smith returned to practice this week and actually had a few solid sessions, per IT’s Eric Nahlin . That backs up what Sarkisian said in that Smith had his best practice of camp shortly before he missed the scrimmage. He returned to action and picked up where he left off in spite of some things not being squared away behind the scenes. In the end, Smith departs Texas having been someone who could have played a large role in the middle of one of the most talented defenses in the country. He might not have started, but he’d have had potential to be a big snap eater as a second-teamer had he stayed. In 2025 as a sophomore, Smith played 450 snaps for the Texas defense. That ranked fourth among Longhorn linebackers behind Anthony Hill , Trey Moore and Liona Lefau . Moore played DE and LB. All three of those players are no longer on the Longhorn roster, so Smith’s rise was right there in front of him. A nagging shoulder injury limited him in the spring and has affected him through the summer and into the fall, however. He has not been fully physically right all year. In the meantime, Texas acquired Pitt transfer Rasheem Biles , a preseason All-American, as well as Florida State’s Justin Cryer . Both of them have had outstanding offseasons to set them up to be Texas’ top two linebackers in 2026. Senior Brad Spence and freshman Tyler Atkinson also figure to play into the rotation this year, and freshman Rocky Cummings has had a strong camp as well. With his health and whatever else on his mind, Smith was a bit lost in the shuffle. He leaves Texas have played in 28 games with one start. He registered 75 tackles, 2.5 sacks, 3 interceptions and 2 forced fumbles. The Jasper, Texas, native has three years of eligibility remaining as a result of the new 5-for-5 rule in the NCAA. This story has been amended from its original form to reflect Smith has left the program.

articles.title: Louisville football: Jeff Brohm pleased with defense, sees areas to improve after second scrimmage
articles.summary: Louiville football coach Jeff Brohm spoke after the Cardinals second scrimmage of fall camp on Friday evening
articles._body: Louisville football coach Jeff Brohm saw plenty to like from his team during its second scrimmage of fall camp on Friday evening, but he also saw a reminder that there is still plenty of work to do before the Cardinals open the season on Sept. 6 against Ole Miss. Unlike last week’s first scrimmage, when the offense had the upper hand, the defense controlled much of Friday’s work. The scrimmage was close to two hours in length for Louisville football. “It was a tale of two scrimmages,” Brohm said after the scrimmage. “The defense dominated today, came out ready to go, very sound in what we did.” The Cardinals’ defense made significant progress in an area Brohm emphasized following the first scrimmage — eliminating big plays. The unit also forced turnovers that Brohm said would have been critical in helping Louisville football win a game. The offense, meanwhile, struggled to match the performance it had last weekend. “Offensively, we were not as sharp,” Brohm said. “We didn’t catch the ball good, we didn’t make great decisions, and we turned the ball over.” Brohm said that is part of the value of scrimmages, particularly when a team is competing against itself. The goal is to identify mistakes, correct them and continue improving before the games begin. “I would love for both sides to play well in a scrimmage; that’s not going to happen,” Brohm said. “One side is going to win, and one side is not, and the defense had the upper hand today.” The second scrimmage provided a positive evaluation of the defense, which Brohm believes has plenty of potential with the experience all over the field. “I think they have a lot of potential,” he said. “We’ve got to coach right; we’ve got to put them in the best position. They’ve got to go execute. . . . But they played a lot better today.” Louisville quarterback Lincoln Kienholz continued to show progress while running the offense. Brohm said Kienholz understands the system, has been making plays with his legs and has done a good job protecting the football. He said he even made some plays with his legs today. “That was a positive,” Brohm said. “That was good to see.” Brohm said the Cardinals will begin shifting more attention toward their season opener against Ole Miss while still incorporating some good-on-good work. He said he’s still excited about this team. “Anytime we can do a game situation where it’s as real as possible, it will help us improve and get better,” Brohm said. “We’ve just got to continue to press forward.”

articles.title: Brenda Song taking Lakers fandom to broadcast booth for Rams-Saints
articles.summary: Brenda Song has already established herself as much more than a celebrity who happens to support Los Angeles sports. Now, the longtime Lakers fanatic will get a chance to put her sports knowledge to work on television. Los Angeles Rams reporter Stu Jackson shared on Aug. 21 that Song will make he
articles._body: Brenda Song has already established herself as much more than a celebrity who happens to support Los Angeles sports. Now, the longtime Lakers fanatic will get a chance to put her sports knowledge to work on television. Los Angeles Rams reporter Stu Jackson shared on Aug. 21 that Song will make her color analyst debut during the Rams’ game against the New Orleans Saints. She will join Jourdan Rodrigue, Rob Havenstein and J.B. Long in the CBS Los Angeles booth for the third quarter. The assignment comes shortly after Song provided plenty of evidence that she knows her stuff, particularly when it comes to Lakers history. I'm being told that @BrendaSong will make her color analyst debut tomorrow. The actress will join @JourdanRodrigue , Rob Havenstein, and @JB_Long in the @CBSLosAngeles booth during the third quarter of Rams vs. Saints. — Stu Jackson (@StuJRams) August 21, 2026 Brenda Song’s Lakers Fandom Runs Deep During an appearance on Mythical Kitchen, Song told Josh Scherer that Kobe Bryant inspired her to watch all 82 Lakers games and own a life-size cutout of the franchise icon. Song really flexed her knowledge when Scherer mentioned Vlade Divac. She quickly noted that Los Angeles dealt Divac in the 1996 trade that landed Bryant. Scherer responded by calling her a “sicko.” “Oh, I’m psychotic. Oh, psychotic,” Song replied. That passion once sent Song to the hospital. She recalled hyperventilating after the Lakers defeated the Sacramento Kings in Game 7 of the 2002 Western Conference Finals, forcing her Kings-supporting family to seek medical attention for her. Bryant remained central to her fandom through his final NBA game in 2016. Song commemorated his 60-point farewell by sharing her 2009 Lakers championship ring on Instagram and calling the moment “the end of an era.” Song will trade basketball memories for football analysis during Rams-Saints, but anyone questioning her credentials as a Los Angeles sports diehard has plenty of evidence to reconsider. articles.title: The Game Responds to Allegations That He Takes Shots at Kendrick Lamar on New Album: ‘Ain’t Diss Nobody on That Song’
articles.summary: The Compton rapper alludes to Kendrick & Drake's beef multiple times on The Documentary III, but claims he's not throwing shots.
articles._body: The Game says he didn’t diss anybody on his new project. The West Coast rapper just dropped The Documentary III , his 11th solo album, and fans feel like he took shots at fellow Compton MC Kendrick Lamar multiple times. He even has Drake featured on a hook. However, The Game denies these claims — although he seemingly mentions Lamar and alludes to Dot’s beef with Drake multiple times on the project. Related The Game Says Rap World Is Missing Drake: ‘This Sh– Is Sad Without Drake in the Club’ The Game Says He Regrets His ‘Womanizing’ Dating History: ‘It Was Just an Exchange’ The Game Picks His Top 100 L.A. Rappers: ‘This My List, Punk!’ Instagram page @obzervetv reposted a rant from user @tyleravilez in which he criticizes Game for “dissing” Kendrick because they’re both from the same city and that he should be taking on more of an “elder” role at this point in his career. “As an L.A. native, we’re supposed to be sticking together, we’re supposed to be showing that we are a unit, and that if you mess with one of us, you mess with all us, and yet you dissin’ one of our own,” he said. “It doesn’t make any sense, bro. Wrap it up.” He added: “At this point in time, you’re supposed to be an elder. You are supposed to helping the youth. Giving people opportunity, so they can get in the rap game and flourish.” The Game then hopped in @obzervetv ‘s comments and said he didn’t diss Kendrick at all. “Ain’t diss nobody on that song loud fa nuthin ahhhh [ninja emoji],” he wrote in a comment that has been pinned. For what it’s worth, on the song “Geezus,” The Game raps, “I say Drake the homie, y’all say it’s treason/ I can’t believe it/ Want me to pick sides while y’all d–kride/ When you’re from the west side you ain’t gotta pick sides…/ I draw led, erase you n—as/ Put that on God, it’s me against all odds/ I’ll pop the steering column on the GNX and wait for n—as.” Then, on “No Brakes” featuring Drake, he mentions picking sides again when he raps, “Me, Drake and a Draco, we the Three Amigos/ N—a said pick a side, then I’m picking homicide,” in reference to the Toronto rapper and Kendrick’s battle in 2024. On “LA Monster,” he alludes to Lamar’s “Boogeyman” moniker and again mentions GNX , the title of Lamar’s 2024-released best rap album Grammy winner. “I ain’t got no problem with the boogeyman/ And he ain’t got a problem with me/ ‘Cause I’ma LA Monster,” he raps and later spits, “I might drive the Rose today/ The GNX scare the hoes away/ ‘Cause I’ma LA Monster.” Finally, on the track titled “The Pen,” he brings Kendrick up again, but this time, he acknowledges the speculation that he’s been throwing shots and says that he hasn’t been. “Like Dr. Dre on the beat/ Yeah, I’m back with that sound/ They say I’m beefing with Kendrick/ How the f— do that sound?” The Game raps, ” ‘Cause I’m feeling like 50 when he made ‘Back Down’/ They say 50 made me, tell him make me again/ I kick myself out the group and make them hate me again.” According to fellow West coast rapper Stat Quo , this all stems from The Game bringing out Drake to Compton to film the music video for their 2015 song “ 100 .” But Stat alleges The Game didn’t take issue with Kendrick working with his old label boss-turned-rival 50 Cent when he made an appearance on Power , so there shouldn’t be any animosity between the two Compton rappers. Go stream The Documentary III and hear for yourself.

articles.title: Nvidia partners with data center developer Cloverleaf
articles.summary: Nvidia continues to pour money into data center development — just as AI data centers bring lots of money into Nvidia.
articles._body: Nvidia is doing everything it can to keep fueling the AI buildout that has underpinned its own good fortunes. On Friday, it announced a partnership with Cloverleaf Infrastructure, a company that lays the groundwork for data centers. Cloverleaf was founded in 2024 and raised $300 million that year. It acts as a kind of middleman between utility companies and data centers, providing power sources and other kinds of pivotal infrastructure for site development. While the companies didn’t disclose terms, the Wall Street Journal reports that Nvidia’s investment in Cloverleaf will likely add up to several hundred million dollars. Reuters reports that the chipmaker now owns a minority stake in the company. TechCrunch reached out to Nvidia for more information. The deal is part of Nvidia’s ongoing push to use its immense profits to keep the AI flywheel spinning. Nvidia is increasingly playing a more direct role in financing and developing the AI data centers that turn around and buy its AI systems. Earlier this week, the company also announced that it would invest $1.5 billion into SB Energy, an OpenAI-linked data center project based in Ohio.

articles._body: This past season, Melvin Council Jr. , in 35 games, averaged 12.7 points, 5.0 rebounds, and 5.1 assists per game. Offensively, he shot 39.2% from the field, 30.8% from behind the arc, and 77.5% from the free-throw line. Before making the move to Kansas, Council, Jr., the Big 12 Newcomer of the Year, spent two years at Monroe College (junior college), one year at Wagner, one year at St. Bonaventure, and, most recently, one year at Kansas. Council, the 6-foot-4, 180-pound guard from Rochester, N.Y., is suing the NCAA in hopes of gaining another year of eligibility. On Friday afternoon, a status hearing took place at the Douglas County District Court. Here’s the latest on the injunction hearing, which is set for September 4. JayhawkSlant.com was in attendance and has the very latest below. — Both sides had representatives on Zoom — Conditions for the September 4 hearing have been set. — Plaintiff expects to call 2 to 3 witnesses. — NCAA expects to call one witness at the September 4 temporary injunction hearing. — Hearing takes between 3 and 6 hours. — Deadline to exchange witness list is August 28, and any stipulations are due September 1. — Everybody will be there in person except the NCAA witness, because of the length of travel so far, and a six-month-old at home (travel considerations). — Mark Oberstaedt (Melvin’s lawyer) plans to file a reply to the NCAA’s response by August 28 because there are some issues Council’s side had not addressed previously. Back on July 27, Kansas head coach Bill Self had this to say about Council and his decision to sue the NCAA for an additional year. “We’re aware of Melvin’s legal efforts to pursue an additional year of Division I eligibility, similar to what a number of student-athletes across the country are doing,” said Self. “At this point, we’re simply monitoring the process and allowing it to play out.”

articles.title: Nneka Ogwumike’s top 7 WNBA career moments
articles.summary: Los Angeles Sparks star Nneka Ogwumike announced on Wednesday that her 15-year professional career will come to an end at the end of the 2026 WNBA season. Ogwumike’s tenure has been remarkable not just because of the points she scored or the awards she collected, but because of the influenc
articles._body: Los Angeles Sparks star Nneka Ogwumike announced on Wednesday that her 15-year professional career will come to an end at the end of the 2026 WNBA season . Ogwumike’s tenure has been remarkable not just because of the points she scored or the awards she collected, but because of the influence she has had on the league as a whole. The first overall pick by the Sparks in the 2012 WNBA Draft, Ogwumike quickly established herself as one of the league’s most consistent and respected players. Over 15 seasons, she’s been a multi-time All-Star, a league MVP, a WNBA champion, and one of the most influential leaders in professional sports. Before her extraordinary career comes to its end, let’s take a look back at some of Ogwumike’s best highlights. Nneka doing a little of everything. 11 PTS | 6 REB | 5 AST pic.twitter.com/ja8OyvNZUJ — Los Angeles Sparks (@LASparks) August 21, 2026 2012: Rookie of the Year Ogwumike immediately proved in her first WNBA season that she belonged among the league’s elite. After being chosen No. 1 out of Stanford, she won the 2012 Rookie of the Year award and was selected to the All-Rookie Team. Her combination of athleticism, efficiency, rebounding, and versatility made her an important member of the Sparks right away. That early success was significant because it established a foundation for a career based on consistency. Ogwumike was not the type of player who had a brief peak — her ROY selection was only the beginning. She developed into one of the W’s most dependable stars and remained highly productive for more than a decade. 2016: Becoming WNBPA P resident Some of Ogwumike’s most important career moments happened away from the basketball court. In 2016, she became president of the Women’s National Basketball Players Association (WNBPA) and has held the position ever since. As union president, Ogwumike helped lead the past year’s high-profile CBA negotiations, which fundamentally changed the professional lives of WNBA players. The agreement significantly improved compensation and benefits for players and represented a major step forward for the league. Ogwumike’s ability to show leadership in the role became especially important during the difficult circumstances surrounding the 2020 Covid season. Ogwumike played a key role in planning the campaign at IMG Academy and helped players navigate the complicated combination of playing basketball, managing health concerns, and social justice activism. Her work demonstrated that being an elite athlete could mean more than just performing on the court. While leading the WNBPA, Ogwumike stepped up as an advocate for the people she played alongside, helping players gain greater control over their careers and working conditions. 2016: MVP and WNBA Championship win If there’s one campaign that stands out in Ogwumike’s career the most, it’s undoubtedly the 2016 season. She won the WNBA MVP award after averaging 19.7 points, 9.1 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 1.3 steals, and 1.2 blocks per game while shooting an astonishing 66.5% from the field. Ogwumike was also awarded with well-earned First-Team All-WNBA and First-Team All-Defensive honors that year. Ogwumike’s consistent efficiency was especially extraordinary. During the season, she set a WNBA record by making 23 consecutive field-goal attempts. She also went 12-for-12 from the field for 32 points against Dallas, setting a record for most made field goals in a game without a miss, and later, she scored a career-high 38 points while shooting 13-for-14 against Atlanta. But her greatest moments came in the playoffs. The Sparks reached the WNBA Finals against the Minnesota Lynx, setting up one of the most memorable championship series in league history. With the championship on the line in Game 5, Ogwumike grabbed an offensive rebound and hit the game-winning jumper with 3.1 seconds remaining, giving Los Angeles a 77-76 victory and its first championship since 2002. That play transformed an already outstanding season into a legendary one. Ogwumike walked away as the WNBA regular season MVP and then delivered the decisive shot to win the championship. 2017: European Championship win with Dynamo Kursk Ogwumike’s accomplishments were not limited to the WNBA, though. During her years playing overseas, she became one of the most successful American players in European basketball. Her most significant international club achievement came with Dynamo Kursk, when she helped the Russian club win the EuroLeague Women championship in 2017. Ogwumike had already established herself as a major force in EuroLeague Women before winning the title. She averaged 17.7 points and 8.9 rebounds per game in the 2015-16 season with Dynamo Kursk, while in 2016-17 she averaged 15.1 points and 10.2 rebounds. Winning the EuroLeague title added another dimension to Ogwumike’s resume. It showed that her skills translated beyond the WNBA and that she could contribute to championship-level teams in a different basketball environment. Combined with her WNBA championship victory the year before, the achievement gave Ogwumike major titles on both sides of the Atlantic and reinforced her status as an international star. 2014, 2018: World Cup gold medals with Team USA That wasn’t the last of Ogwumike’s major international career accomplishments. She won two senior FIBA World Cup gold medals with the United States, helping Team USA capture championships in both 2014 and 2018. At the 2014 FIBA World Championship for Women in Istanbul, Türkiye, Team USA went undefeated and beat Spain in the gold-medal game. Ogwumike contributed throughout the tournament, averaging 7.5 points and 4.8 rebounds per contest. Four years later, she was again part of an American championship team at the 2018 FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup in Tenerife, Spain.
