articles.title: Leydecker leaves no doubt, headlines six Hawkeyes at U20 Worlds
articles.summary: After six days of competition in Bratislava, Slovakia the Iowa Hawkeyes are heading home from the U20 World Championships. They do so with a gold medal and several laudable efforts in tow after waging 19 collective matches against the best young wrestlers in the world. For all of them, the lessons l
articles._body: After six days of competition in Bratislava, Slovakia the Iowa Hawkeyes are heading home from the U20 World Championships. They do so with a gold medal and several laudable efforts in tow after waging 19 collective matches against the best young wrestlers in the world. For all of them, the lessons learned will carry far beyond this week-long overseas excursion. And whether they accomplished their ultimate goal or left wanting more, it can only benefit their future pursuits if they apply the experience wisely. Of course, if your name is Everest Leydecker, you might not want to change a darn thing. After all, winning a second consecutive World title in dominant fashion would seem to indicate that you’re already on the right track. Everest climbed the U20 World bracket… again. @USAWrestling pic.twitter.com/VHBOQYdrcv — Iowa Women's Wrestling (@IowaW_Wrestling) August 20, 2026 The 18-year-old freshman is now 8-0 at the past two editions of this event – outscoring her opponents by a combined margin of 70-4. In fact, Leydecker hasn’t suffered an international defeat since winning U20 Worlds a year ago – and it’s not for a lack of competing, nor elite competition. She’ll step onto campus next week in as fine of form as any incoming Hawkeye in school history. And she’s still got U23 and Senior World titles to pursue later this fall. All told, Leydecker led a quartet of Hawkeyes on the U.S. women’s freestyle team that placed fourth in Slovakia . Women’s Freestyle Results Everest Leydecker – gold at 55kg Taylor Whiting – 5 th at 53kg Karlee Brooks – 5 th at 57kg Bella Williams – 7 th at 62kg Meanwhile, Leister Bowling IV followed up his 2025 fifth place showing by finishing tenth for the U.S. in the Greco-Roman discipline. And 2028 commit Fred Bachmann made his U20 debut for Puerto Rico in Men’s Freestyle. Here are all the highlights from the week that was. Leydecker puts pin(s) in repeat 55kg title There’s really not much left to say about Everest Leydecker, so what if I show you instead? How about dominating (then pinning) a reigning U23 World silver medalist to kick things off – and from an improbable position, no less? Everest Leydecker is something else… The Iowa freshman starts her quest for back-to-back U20 titles with a FALL over Hansika Lamba – sticking the reigning U23 World medalist from a crazy/crafty position. Next up shortly: the 55kg quarterfinals. by @FloWrestling pic.twitter.com/RBeIXb8ANv — Tanner Lafever (@TannerLafever) August 19, 2026 The Iowa freshman followed that with a far more conventional quarterfinal pin – sticking former U17 World silver medalist Valeryia Mikitsich (Belarus) after building a 10-0 first-period lead. Now one win away from a repeat finals appearance, Leydecker wasn’t about to let up. And while the final score over U20 Asian runner up Meilin Zhou (China) may have only read 8-0, the performance was utterly comprehensive and controlled: A winner by 12-0 and 11-0 tech. fall to reach the semifinal, Zhou never once sniffed a threatening attack against the young American – who did what she wanted and scored when she wanted for the full six minutes. Finals bound once again, Leydecker’s last test would be her greatest. The challenger – Japan’s Nana Kozuka – had displayed similar dominance to that point. In fact, pre-finals the former U17 World silver medalist’s scoring differential (28-2) was quite similar to Leydecker’s (25-0). Now, the two would settle it on the mat. In the early going, Kozuka dictated the action – striking on a low double that, after a prolonged scramble, eventually led to an exposure. Upon restart, she went right back to the same maneuver – only this time Leydecker managed to hold for a stalemate. As the opening period waned, the Hawkeye began to settle in. And a late step out made it 2-1 at the break. After taking instructions in the corner from her father, Randy, and Iowa head coach Clarissa Chun, Leydecker returned to center with three minutes to find a win. And as it turned out, most of that time would be spent methodically closing in on a second World title. Everest Leydecker reached the highest U20 peak again, securing a fall in the World gold medal 55 kg finals. pic.twitter.com/kXorc32TK0 — FloWrestling (@FloWrestling) August 20, 2026 Right off the whistle Kozuka shot yet another low double. But on this occasion Leydecker had it stymied before quickly transitioning into a reattack of her own. A takedown secured, she kept hold of Kozuka’s leg for an additional exposure – then exploited the compromising position to pursue the fall. Nearly two minutes later, having slowly but steadily improved her position on her desperate opponent, Leydecker finally heard the slap of the mat followed by a chorus of cheers. She was a World champion once again – becoming just the fourth-ever American woman to win twice at the U20 level . Here’s what the first-year Hawkeye had to say following her gold medal performance: Brooks fights for fifth at 57kg No Hawkeye was busier in Slovakia this week than Karlee Brooks – whose five matches equaled her fifth-place finish at 57kg. The Iowa junior began her tournament with consecutive bonus point wins. Up first, a 10-0 clinic over Poland’s Julia Gibalska – which Brooks would follow with a tougher, though eventual 12-2 technical fall victory over Yu Cheng (TPE): Here are the highlights from Brooks’ Round of 16 win: via @FloWrestling pic.twitter.com/1VZauG1a7l — Tanner Lafever (@TannerLafever) August 20, 2026 That preceded a quarterfinal final matchup against eventual champion Konami Ono – who, once upon a time, stopped by to train in the Iowa room for a few days. (If you aren’t aware, the Iowa women’s program has pretty strong domestic and international pull.) As were all comers against Ono, Brooks was felled in bonus-point fashion – but was subsequently pulled into repechage as her Japanese foe’s tour de force continued through the finals. As the Heat are led by Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo, the team has now made a m
articles._body: With the Miami Heat expected to sign star Klay Thompson , it is one of the many moves made this offseason that has shifted the direction of the team, including the blockbuster trade for superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo. As the Heat are led by Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo , the team has now made a move when it comes to the coaching staff, as it’ll be one that the former Milwaukee Bucks big man will love. According to NBA insider Chris Haynes, assistant coach Vin Baker will be on Erik Spoelstra’s coaching staff after being with Milwaukee for the last eight seasons. Haynes would note that Antetokounmpo and Baker have a “close bond,” as it is a move that could help the star with the transition after being with the Bucks for 13 seasons and the only familiar face being Bobby Portis Jr., who was in the aforementioned trade. “After spending eight seasons with [the] Milwaukee Bucks as an assistant, Vin Baker is joining Erik Spoelstra’s coaching staff with [the] Miami Heat to reunite with Giannis Antetokounmpo to whom he has a close bond with, sources tell me,” Haynes wrote on X, formerly Twitter. Before being an assistant coach in the NBA, Baker was a former player in the league, starting his career with Milwaukee after he was selected with the eighth overall pick in the 1993 NBA Draft. Playing with other teams such as the Seattle SuperSonics, Boston Celtics, New York Knicks, and others, Baker was a four-time All-Star and had a productive NBA career. At any rate, Baker now takes his coaching duties to Miami, as the team looks to usher in a new era with Antetokounmpo at the forefront. articles.title: Red Wings’ Moritz Seider still appreciates Steve Yzerman for giving him a chance in 2019
articles.summary: The Detroit Red Wings are still searching for a new general manager as training camp approaches. Detroit moved on from Steve Yzerman shortly after 2026 NHL free agency began. For all the conversation surrounding Yzerman’s work in Detroit, he still has a supporter in defenseman Moritz Seider
articles._body: The Detroit Red Wings are still searching for a new general manager as training camp approaches. Detroit moved on from Steve Yzerman shortly after 2026 NHL free agency began. For all the conversation surrounding Yzerman’s work in Detroit, he still has a supporter in defenseman Moritz Seider. The superstar defenseman was the first draft pick of the Yzerman era for the Red Wings. It was a bit of a stunning move at the time, taking the German defenseman higher than many draft analysts had him. However, it turned out to be one of his best moves, and Seider remains grateful to this day . “I can only say how thankful I am for his opportunity back in ’19, where he saw something in me a lot of people didn’t see at the time,” Seider said of Yzerman, via The Athletic. “He took a big risk putting my name on this board that early, and I think that’s something that obviously makes my connection a little bit more special with him, and that’s something I’ll always really be thankful for.” Seider has emerged as one of the best all-around defensemen in the NHL. This past season saw him stamp his claim to being the best defensive defenseman in the league. He finished with 2.18 even-strength defensive WAR, according to HockeyStats.com. This is not only the best mark in the league for 2025-26, but he was also the only defenseman worth at least 2.0 even-strength defensive WAR. The Red Wings are going through a lot off the ice heading into the 2026-27 season. Seider remains, as do some impressive young players. Perhaps the superstar defenseman can steady the ship and lead Detroit to its next playoff run sooner rather than later. articles._body: UNLV transfer forward Kimani Hamilton has signed with Mississippi State , On3’s Pete Nakos reports. Hamilton began his collegiate career at Mississippi State (2022-23). As a freshman, Hamilton appeared in 12 games for the Bulldogs. There, he averaged just 2.6 points in seven minutes per game. He then transferred to High Point , where he played from 2023-25. As a member of the HPU program, Hamilton transformed into a major contributor. In 71 games for the Panthers, Hamilton averaged 14.0 points, 5.9 rebounds, and 2.3 assists. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Last season, Hamilton played for Josh Pastner ‘s UNLV Rebels. In 35 games, Hamilton averaged 12.8 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 2.3 assists. Now, he’ll return to the Mississippi State program as the Bulldogs seek a return to the NCAA Tournament after missing the field last season. Mississippi State head coach Chris Jans heads into his fifth season with the program. In that span, Jans has led the Bulldogs to a 76-59 (29-43) record with three NCAA Tournament appearances. Preliminary injunction for 2022 class opens door Judge  Charlotte Sweeney  of the U.S. District Court of Colorado granted a class-wide preliminary injunction that required the NCAA to declare eligible all high school class of 2022 athletes who exhausted four seasons of eligibility this spring, according to documents obtained by On3’s  Pete Nakos . “All persons in the United States who began to play in collegiate sports in the 2022-2023 season, competed in NCAA Division I sports, and completed four years of eligibility as defined by the NCAA’s prior rules by the conclusion of the 2025-2026 season, and are therefore barred from playing a fifth season due to the NCAA’s adoption and immediate implementation of the Five-Year Eligibility Rule,” the class certification read. Hamilton is one of many players from the Class of 2022 that was granted an extra year of eligibility, which he will now use to suit up for the Bulldogs once again. A few other notable names to receive the extra year include former Michigan State forward Jaxon Kohler (committed to BYU ), former UCLA guard Donovan Dent , former Missouri forward Mark Mitchell , and former Ole Miss guard AJ Storr (committed to UNLV ). To keep up with the latest players on the move, check out On3’s Transfer Portal  wire . West Virginia head coach Rich Rodriguez addressed the media following practice Friday evening and WVSports.com provides a summary of what was said. –Rodriguez said that Bryan Hansen at punter, they wanted a proven guy and he has been booming the ball. In the last week, it’s been amazing how he is doing and he is an outstanding holder. Jack Cassidy has a strong leg and has been booming it through the end zone on kickoffs. –Cassidy and Nate Flower are ahead in the kicker race. –Sunday they will have a depth chart meeting to see where everybody is at heading into next week. –Rodriguez said that if there is somebody dynamic, they will put them at kick return. He wants to have the confidence in his return units to bring it out. –Defense is doing more stuff than they ever have. Most of it has been things they need all year but they want to do a whole lot. He’s demanding from a schematic understanding standpoint. They do a lot more stuff than most but if they can’t execute it he will step in and pin it down. –Rodriguez said if players are willing, you can coach toughness in them. But if they’re not naturally tough they have to be at least willing to attempt to be that. He’s had guys that have proven him wrong. Guys will adapt to the environment and there is a certain degree of toughness you need to have to be in this program. –Little more situational stuff with the scrimmage this time. A minute in the game, red zone, etc. They did a whole bunch of that yesterday and tomorrow will be the same. He doesn’t want to assume all of the players have been in those situations. –Coastal Carolina has a whole new staff with a bunch of new players and a lot of guesswork there. It’s the first game so you will likely see a whole bunch of new stuff. But there’s a lot of things that West Virginia is doing that they haven’t done before. You have to be foundational and fundamentally strong. –Rodriguez said everybody has a system and they have an answer sheet in all three phases if the opponent does something. You have to have answers for it all. That is something they will finalize in the next three to four days and to get the players to anticipate what those answers will be. — Scotty Fox has played some in the system but the others haven’t really done that. When you grow up in the system, they can anticipate what the answers are going to be and it becomes natural. –Rodriguez would like to have an extra week of practice, but the players want to play a game. He runs like a tight end. Emerson Joy has great size and first thing he said to him was you know you have four downs here because he was Canadian. But Rodriguez thinks he can help. –Muya loves ball and you can see him on his day off putting in extra work. — Cam Torbor was a great find for them but they knew about him from his time in Alabama. He’s done an outstanding job and he’s going to play. He is really excited about him. He has size and speed and might be the fastest linebacker they’ve got. — Prince Strachan and John Neider , Taron Francis have come on. Keon Hutchins is one of the fastest guys they’ve got. articles.title: How AI accounting startup Rillet raised $100M and became a unicorn in 48 hours
articles.summary: Rillet CEO Nicolas Kopp shared growth numbers at a board meeting and set off a fundraising frenzy from Iconiq, Sequoia and others. Without even trying.
articles._body: Rillet co-founder and CEO Nicolas Kopp seems justifiably confident as we talk over Zoom a day after his company announced a $100 million raise at a $1 billion valuation. The U.S. has a shortage of accountants right now, which is driving growth of his AI-native accounting platform so much, he raised that cash in 48 hours without even trying. Rillet emerged from stealth two years ago. Since then, it has raised $200 million from top investors like Iconiq, Andreessen Horowitz, and Sequoia. It’s also amassed 600 customers, most of whom are looking to ditch legacy accounting systems like Oracle and NetSuite, Kopp says. A few weeks ago, Rillet held a board meeting and shared with investors its growth since its $70 million Series B last summer. Annualized revenue rate had doubled in the last quarter alone; the startup added new clients, many of them public companies, and an alliance with EY to introduce AI tools to the auditing giant. His customers aren’t piloting Rillet either, he said — they’re yanking out ERP and accounting software from competitors like Intuit, NetSuite, or Oracle. After that board meeting, text messages were fired, calls were made, and 48 hours later, Rillet was a unicorn. The company wasn’t even looking to raise, Kopp said. Seth Pierrepont, the general partner at Iconiq who led the round, said that the deal came together fast but “it wasn’t a cold start,” he described. “Rillet had already proven it could win against the incumbents that have owned this category for decades,” Pierrepont told TechCrunch. Iconiq also co-led the company’s Series B, and with this latest round, Pierrepont joins the Rillet board. “A year of watching the team deliver on that made doubling down and leading the Series C an easy call.” Julien Bek, Sequoia’s lead investor on the deal, also said that, though 48 hours might look rushed from the outside, from their perspective, re-investing in Rillet was a “very easy decision,” after the company’s growth in the past year. “Rillet’s initial wedge is accounting, but ultimately they are reinventing the entire finance function,” Bek told TechCrunch, adding that agentic finance could become “one of the largest application software opportunities of the AI era.” Sequoia led Rillet’s Series A last summer. “When the opportunity came together,” Bek continued. “We already had all the context we needed.” Rillet is one of many AI-native startups now giving legacy players a run for relevance. Earlier this year, software stocks on the public market dipped as investors worried about how emerging AI tools would affect them. Kopp thinks there’s some truth to that. “AI is going to come hard at these legacy players,” he said, because it is giving customers compelling alternatives. Rillet, for example, was built for AI agents, not humans, letting humans work alongside the AI agents on corporate bookkeeping. Rillet clients range from laundromats to a major sports franchise. Some 50% of Rillet customers come from Intuit, 30% from NetSuite and Sage Intacct, and 20% from Oracle, SAP, Workday, and Microsoft products, he said. Security is critical when working with sensitive client data, Kopp said. Rillet includes model routing, so customers can redirect requests to the foundational model of their choice (like OpenAI or Anthropic), and Rillet’s harness prevents these models from training on their data, he says. There’s also no cross-training — meaning one customer’s data remains proprietary. The agents also have memory, so they can remember and store historical actions they can then use for their own process and improvement. About three months ago, Rillet released a governance feature letting accountants see and audit every decision the AI agent has made — including what numbers the agents pull and how they calculated them. Creating this was harder than it looks, Kopp said, because the team had to compress agent data into a format humans could understand. Kopp said this feature was only possible to build recently because AI agents have gotten so powerful so quickly. They can, for example, now support multi-step workflows over longer periods of time. Because of that, auditing what they are doing has become even more important for clients. “We barely scratched the surface of potential and opportunity that this technology has,” he said. Right now, regulations for public companies require that every transaction made by an AI agent be approved by another human. He thinks regulators and top names are watching how the accounting industry evolves around this new technology. He’s hopeful that new rules and regulations will evolve that align more with where everything is headed. “It’s a very normal process,” he said. “Similar to when the cloud came, of just getting everybody familiar with what’s going on and how it helps the profession.” Kopp also doesn’t think mass job displacement from AI is coming anytime soon, especially in accounting. (Stanford released a report a few weeks ago that found no widespread job displacement yet.) He insists that Rillet isn’t a human replacement, not even for junior accountants. They can use Rillet to help automate and assist with some of the profession’s grunt work. He also pointed out the expected shortage of accountants in the U.S. The number of those graduating with an accounting degree has been declining since at least 2010. In a recent report, the Controllers Council Organization found that 61% of finance leaders have struggled to find finance, accounting, and CPA talent in the past year. The pullback is not entirely shocking: accountants’ hours are long, the pipeline to the top is arduous, the pay often doesn’t match the workload, and the work doesn’t appeal to everyone. At the same time, the Bureau of Labor Statistics has projected that accounting-related needs are expected to grow by at least 5%, adding 72,800 jobs by 2034. articles.title: Shaq wanted to join the Avengers but Marvel saw one big problem
articles.summary: Shaquille O’Neal spent years trying to add the Marvel Cinematic Universe to a résumé that already included a turn as a DC superhero. His size was not the problem. His fame was. Speaking with Variety while promoting his “Dunkman” league, O’Neal revealed that Marvel declined his push for an “Avenge
articles._body: Shaquille O’Neal spent years trying to add the Marvel Cinematic Universe to a résumé that already included a turn as a DC superhero. His size was not the problem. His fame was. Speaking with Variety while promoting his “Dunkman” league, O’Neal revealed that Marvel declined his push for an “Avengers” appearance because audiences would immediately see Shaq rather than the character. “I wanted to be in the ‘Avengers,’” O’Neal said. According to him, studio officials appreciated the idea but believed fans would shout, “Hey, that’s Shaq!” as soon as his face appeared. The 54-year-old first publicly campaigned for a place in the franchise during a 2018 interview with EW. Despite portraying the title character in 1997’s “Steel,” O’Neal never crossed into Marvel’s world and will not appear in December’s “Avengers: Doomsday.” Shaquille O'Neal says he asked Marvel if he could be in an ‘AVENGERS’ movie but was turned down. “They were like, ‘Shaq, we fuckin’ love you and we’d love to put you in, but if your face pops up on screen people are going to go, ‘Hey, that’s Shaq!’” (Source:… pic.twitter.com/aLIH5kzFlu — DiscussingFilm (@DiscussingFilm) August 21, 2026 Shaq discovers the cost of being Shaq O’Neal said the issue extends beyond Marvel. He wants more action parts, but leading Hollywood executives have told him that his celebrity overwhelms any fictional identity he tries to adopt. “I would love to do more action roles,” he explained, adding that casting directors consider him “too big” for moviegoers to accept him as someone else. That enormous public persona continues to work elsewhere. “Dunkman” calls itself the first professional league dedicated to dunking, with international contestants pursuing a $500,000 prize. TNT will air the finals on Aug. 25. Marvel can explain gods, aliens and entire multiverses. Convincing audiences that Shaq is not Shaq apparently proved too ambitious. As head coach Lane Kiffin leads the LSU football team into a new era, there is no denying that many will have opinions on [&#
articles._body: With the LSU football program gearing up for the 2026 season , the team has landed an interesting player who was with the Notre Dame Fighting Irish for the last four years. As head coach Lane Kiffin leads the LSU football team into a new era , there is no denying that many will have opinions on the latest addition. According to Pete Thamel of ESPN, the latest commitment to the Tigers comes from defensive end Junior Tuihalamaka, as he has just been ruled eligible for a fifth year after a recent court ruling in Louisiana. “NEWS: Notre Dame transfer defensive end Junior Tuihalamaka has committed to LSU, per his agent Noah Reisenfeld of 21 Sports & Entertainment. Tuihalamaka is eligible for a fifth year of college football from the state court ruling in Louisiana on Thursday,” Thamel wrote on X, formerly Twitter. News broke on Thursday when a judge in Louisiana granted a year of eligibility to Tuihalamaka and 15 other players in the class of 2022, thanks to a restraining order. With the news, Tuihalamaka entered the transfer portal, which is how it led him to play for the LSU football team. The Tigers add a player who totaled 60 tackles and four tackles for loss in his career. Tuihalamaka is part of the group of players who have been granted another year of college football eligibility, but he might not be the most famous. In a drastic turn of events, one of the players who have the ability to return to college football is former Ole Miss tight end Dae’Quan Wright, who entered the transfer portal, though he was already on the Cleveland Browns roster. articles.title: Ex-Gold Glover makes feelings crystal clear after Mariners’ Kade Anderson promotion
articles.summary: The Seattle Mariners (60-68) have crashed into the rocks during the second half of the 2026 season, and now they are frantically trying to patch up the holes and prepare their vessel for an inauspicious yet still possible voyage into the MLB playoffs. Since there is no quick fix for their greates
articles._body: The Seattle Mariners (60-68) have crashed into the rocks during the second half of the 2026 season, and now they are frantically trying to patch up the holes and prepare their vessel for an inauspicious yet still possible voyage into the MLB playoffs. Since there is no quick fix for their greatest area of weakness — the lineup — president of baseball operations Jerry Dipoto is attempting to reinforce this franchise’s pitch-first identity. Prized left-hander Kade Anderson is joining the big-league roster and will make his debut in Saturday night’s game against the Chicago Cubs. The No. 5 overall prospect , per MLB.com, could infuse much-needed energy into the team and fan base, but he can only compensate so much for the Mariners’ putrid offense. A 2017 World Series champion and 2012 Gold Glove winner was brutally honest about Seattle’s current situation . “You’re providing an elite pitcher to an already pretty elite pitching staff, with some starts here and there going a little haywire, but it all comes back to hitting,” Houston Astros analyst and retired right fielder Josh Reddick said on Friday’s edition of the “Foul Territory” podcast. “He can’t help boost the lineup’s numbers if he’s only pitching. “He’s gonna strike out guys, maybe give up one or no runs and he’s gonna get a no-decision after going six or seven innings, and hopefully praying that they can win the ballgame. Obviously, you’re very happy for the kid and he’s deserving of every call-up that he’s getting, but you gotta hit. Hopefully, this can be a boost for the whole clubhouse and not just the pitching staff.” Calling up Kade Anderson is great, but the Mariners still need to HIT, says @JRedDubDeuce . "Hopefully this can be a boost for the whole clubhouse and not just the pitching staff." pic.twitter.com/Ig7qms0Go7 — Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) August 21, 2026 Some fans will dismiss Reddick as an Astros homer, but he is being quite fair to Seattle in his assessment. The Mariners are underachieving to a startling degree this season. They are last in MLB with 500 runs scored and 156 doubles and rank 29th in OPS, batting average and slugging percentage. The pitching staff has not been as sharp as expected, sitting in 11th in ERA (4.00), so there is a chance that Anderson will make the M’s a more competitive squad down the stretch. But Seattle’s ceiling will remain painfully limited unless its top hitters start performing. MVP runner-up and record-breaking catcher Cal Raleigh is batting .156 with 13 home runs through 392 plate appearances. Julio Rodriguez has yet to produce one of his signature summer explosions and owns a modest .733 OPS this season. Josh Naylor is hovering around league average after signing a five-year, $92.5 million contract last November. Cole Young is plummeting amid a rough August and fellow former first-round draft pick Colt Emerson is languishing below the Mendoza Line. Randy Arozarena and Dominic Canzone are enjoying standout campaigns, but the Mariners are collectively failing to build on their historic 2025 season . Kade Anderson has the daunting task of helping them avoid complete embarrassment. Perhaps he can take a couple of swings in batting practice. articles.title: Smart Money Helping Support Bitcoin Rebound, Says Pantera Capital
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Smart Money Helping Support Bitcoin Rebound, Says Pantera Capital American investment firm Pantera Capital’s portfolio manager has said “smart money” is helping push bitcoin’s price higher.  Cosmo Jiang, portfolio manager at the firm, said in a Friday CNBC interview that the next resistance for the coin’s price could be around $80,000 and that while small pullback was possible, “smart money” was now flooding into the space.  Bitcoin surged this week on positive regulatory news coming out of the U.S. and news that the Treasury Department would at least double the size of its long-dated bond buybacks. JUST IN: $3.8 billion Pantera Capital tells CNBC the Bitcoin price is starting to “reverse” to the upside "There's smart money now coming in, and there's real fundamentals to support the rebound in prices.” pic.twitter.com/278fR8t9vx — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) August 21, 2026 “From everything we see, positioning is starting to reverse,” Jiang said.  “People are going from very much on the sidelines and even net short positioning to now realizing they want to be long, for what could be a very big technology.” Bitcoin was recently priced at $77,412 after surging more than 23% over the past week. The biggest cryptocurrency touched as high as $79,319 earlier on Friday.  While spending most of June and July below $65,000, bitcoin has benefited from news that came out of the White House this week. President Donald Trump held a meeting with crypto executives earlier in the week, and urged lawmakers to get the long-awaited Clarity Act over the line.  The crypto legislation, which aims to make it clear which digital assets the SEC and CFTC will watchdog, has been called for by industry bigwigs for years. A vote will now go ahead on the proposed law in September.  Bitcoin surged on Trump’s comments. On the same day, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the department would at least double the size of its long-dated bond buybacks.  Non-yielding assets including bitcoin and gold jumped on the news.  Jiang added that a slew of positive fundamentals in the crypto space — including stablecoin adoption, prediction markets, perpetual futures, and “the crossover of AI” — would help push bitcoin’s price higher.  “It’s really hard not to be bullish,” he said. This post Smart Money Helping Support Bitcoin Rebound, Says Pantera Capital first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .

The #Texans are signing veteran WRs Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones, sources tell me
articles._body: The Houston Texans are intent on playing dominant football this season. Not only do they have a goal of winning the AFC South title, they want to represent the AFC and go to their first Super Bowl in team history. The #Texans are signing veteran WRs Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones, sources tell me and @RapSheet . Both impressed in a workout today and join the mix in Houston after the loss of Jayden Higgins to a torn ACL. pic.twitter.com/oYlmSVJ4BT — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) August 21, 2026 The Texans believe they have the experience and the talent to get to the top of the conference, and one of their strengths is the talent in their passing game. They are counting on quarterback C.J. Stroud having an excellent year and making the kind of key throws at the most crucial moments that allow the Texans to win games in the fourth quarter. The Texans are under the strong impression that they have the depth at the WR spot with Nico Collins and Jaylin Noel to get the job done, but they took a serious blow during the team’s combined practice session with the Las Vegas Raiders. Jayden Higgins, the third WR in the Texans’ offense suffered a torn ACL in Tuesday’s practice that will sideline him throughout the season. As a result of that injury, the Texans have signed WRs Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones to battle for a receiving position — possibly a starting slot — in the finals 10 days of training camp. Shepard and Jones both were impressive in Friday workouts and that merited contract offers by the team. Higgins was expected to be a key part of the Texans attack this season. He had 41 catches for 525 yards and 6 touchdowns last year. He regularly used his size, strength and big body to wall off defenders and make crucial receptions. The Football Association’s Full-Time platform lists the eight-time Olympic gold medalist on the roster for Wythenshawe FC Veterans, per The Guardian. The Greater Ma
articles._body: Usain Bolt may soon trade the track for the pitch once again, this time alongside a collection of recognizable Premier League names. The Football Association’s Full-Time platform lists the eight-time Olympic gold medalist on the roster for Wythenshawe FC Veterans, per The Guardian. The Greater Manchester club competes in the Cheshire Veterans League, although Bolt’s appearance on the website does not guarantee that he will play. Former Manchester City midfielder Stephen Ireland manages a squad featuring Danny Drinkwater, Antonio Valencia, Emile Heskey, Joleon Lescott, Marc Albrighton, Nedum Onuoha and Papiss Cisse. Together, last season’s group brought more than 1,800 Premier League appearances to the Sunday league level. The fastest man in the world will play Sunday league football The FA's Full-Time website shows Usain Bolt as a registered player for Wythenshawe, an over-35s team based in south Manchester pic.twitter.com/4Te7QdG3wk — ESPN FC (@ESPNFC) August 21, 2026 Bolt never abandoned his football dream The Jamaican superstar retired from sprinting after the 2017 World Championships, leaving the sport as the record holder in both the 100-meter and 200-meter events. Football soon became his next pursuit. Bolt spent time with Australia’s Central Coast Mariners and scored twice in a 2018 friendly. He later agreed to professional terms, but his stint ended eight weeks afterward. He stepped away from his playing ambitions in early 2019. Still, Bolt never drifted far from the game. The lifelong Manchester United supporter has regularly competed in Soccer Aid, giving fans occasional reminders of his speed and enthusiasm on the pitch. Bolt once advised young players to surround themselves with trustworthy people, remain disciplined and continue working even when success takes time. He closed that 2017 FIFA interview with a fitting personal motto: “Anything is possible.” At 40, Bolt could soon put that belief to another test. A Sunday league appearance would hardly match an Olympic final, but few athletes could make it feel like a major event. articles.title: In Canada: Drake Dominates 80% of Spotify’s Global Impact List for the First Half of 2026
articles.summary: Also up north this week: Montreal's LASSO country festival sees rapid growth and Drizzy celebrates the opening of Ottowa's newest music hub.
articles._body: Drake continues to rule streaming. After being crowned Spotify’s most-streamed artist in Canada last year, the streaming service has released its Global Impact List for the first half of 2026, revealing the 50 most-played songs by Canadian artists outside of their home country. To no one’s surprise, the Toronto rapper has 40 of the 50 spots, including the top 12. Thanks to the rapper’s historic  Iceman  release — which included a triple-album drop with Maid of Honour and Habibti — Drake commands a whopping 80% of the list, led by his chart-topping hit, “Janice SFTU,” which the streaming platform already tapped as one of its  song-of-the-summer contenders . It’s followed by “National Treasures,” “Shabang,” “Whisper My Name” and “Ran To Atlanta,” featuring Future and Molly Santana, to round out the top 5. He wraps up the list, too, with “Rust Intro” at No. 50. Related Here’s Why Drake Fans Think New Music Could Be on the Way HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery BE:FIRST Is Ready for the World: Inside the J-Pop Superstars' Long-Planned U.S. Breakthrough The remaining artists on the list boast a diverse lineup of homegrown acts, spanning genres including country, indie rock, Punjabi, hip-hop and electronic.  Cameron Whitcomb is the highest-ranking act after Drake, landing at No. 13 with his viral track “Kingdom of Fear,” another track that the streaming service listed as a song-of-the-summer contender. It has become a big moment for the B.C. artist, securing his  first top 3 hit on the Billboard Canadian Hot 100  chart dated Aug. 22. Whitcomb earns a second entry on the Spotify list at No. 49 with “You and Me.” In recent years, the growing influence of Punjabi-Canadian artists on the world stage has become a major force. While the second half of 2025’s list featured multiple tracks by Karan Aujla and Ikky, they’re passing the torch to Shubh , who claims two entries on the 2026 list. He arrives at No. 23 with “Moves” and “Bounce” at No. 35. It’s a welcome return for the Punjabi-Canadian act, who was on Spotify’s first-ever Global Impact List in 2025 . Viral act  bbno$  lands at No. 41 with “diamonds are forever.” It’s been a year of transformation for the Vancouver-based artist, born Alex Gumuchian, who has found success with his independent project over the past couple of years. At No. 43, viral Quebec duo Angine de Poitrine makes their first and only appearance on the list with “Fabienk,” arguably the group’s biggest hit  from their album,  Vol. II . The buzzy math rock group has made a  global breakthrough  with their polka-dot ensembles and unique sound. Rounding out the list is what Spotify calls “a diverse cross-section of Canadian talent,” including: Toronto indie-rockers Good Kid with “Cicada” (No. 29), producer Murda Beatz’s Prospa-featuring track “Baby” (No. 33), Korean-Canadian rapper OXYNOVA’s “SSSAK” (No. 34) and Vancouver-based producer Asad Khan’s remix “Piya Ghar Aaya” (No. 39). Read more  here . —  H.T.S. Montreal’s LASSO Festival Grows Rapidly Alongside Canada’s Country Music Scene It’s not every day that Montreal’s public transit is filled with cowboy hats, Canadian tuxedos and Western belt buckles. Now, that’s a yearly mid-August tradition for country music lovers as LASSO celebrates its fifth edition. The large-scale country music festival, co-produced by Evenko and Live Nation, welcomed over 43,000 fans this year on August 15 and 16. The lineup featured headliners Thomas Rhett and Mumford & Sons, along with established country acts like Carly Pearce, The Band Perry, Old Dominion and Jon Pardi and rising Canadian stars like Cameron Whitcomb, Morgan Griffiths and Noah Brigden. Related In Canada: Osheaga Festival Draws Near-Record Attendance With Tate McRae, Stella Lefty & More Nick Farkas , Evenko’s senior vice-president of booking, concerts and events, says it’s a rapidly growing success story that has grown faster than other major festivals like Osheaga (which he co-founded ). “Five years in, where this festival is at, for me, is just fantastic,” Farkas says. “We were not this far along on any festival we’ve ever done. It’s a ton of fun to work on it.” The festival’s growth fits into a bigger trend of country music throughout the music landscape. Recently, the genre has surpassed hip-hop and pop as the most successful genre at the top of the charts. This week, the Billboard Canadian Hot 100 features a rare sweep of country songs comprising the top four slots, with Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” at No. 1, Stella Lefty’s “Boston” at No. 2, Cameron Whitcomb’s “Kingdom of Fear” at No. 3 and Morgan Wallen’s “Been By Now” at No. 4. That potential was first bubbling when LASSO began five years ago, but it was unforeseen in Canada just five years before that. “We had one arena country show every few years,” Farkas explains. “[The scene] was non-existent, and we had no country radio, so it was not on anyone’s radar. We started seeing a shift when we booked a show with Luke Bryan in 2016 and it sold out the Bell Centre in like a day. We were like, “Holy crap, that’s, there’s something going on here with some of this newer country stuff.” Evenko later rolled the dice with a large-scale festival, combining the rising global appeal of country music with the Quebec and Canadian scene, giving local country musicians a global stage and spotlight that didn’t previously exist in the metropolis. This year, Lasso saw a record 30% turnout from outside Quebec, a “huge win,” per Farkas, that has cemented the festival’s nationwide and international reputation. articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles have a few questions surrounding their defense before the season begins, and it surrounds the health of Jonathan Greenard. The edge rusher is dealing with a pec injury that could force him to miss the start of the season, as there is uncertainty about when he’ll be b
articles._body: The Philadelphia Eagles have a few questions surrounding their defense before the season begins, and it surrounds the health of Jonathan Greenard. The edge rusher is dealing with a pec injury that could force him to miss the start of the season, as there is uncertainty about when he’ll be back on the field. For now, the Eagles may have to find some help to fill his void, and there are talks that they could be interested in bringing back Haason Reddick, according to Bleacher Report. “A reunion would make sense, as Jonathan Greenard is now dealing with a pectoral injury and could miss the start of the regular season,” Bleacher Report wrote. Reddick played for the Eagles in 2022 and 2023, and he played his best football in those two seasons. He finished with 16 sacks in 2022 and 11 in 2023, and afterwards played for the New York Jets and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. It’s uncertain if the Eagles will be able to get the production that he gave them a few years ago, but it’s good that he’ll be back somewhere he’s familiar. The Eagles have had one of the better defensive lines over the past few seasons, and they’ve been led by Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter . They traded for Greenard during the offseason and signed him to a four-year, $98 million extension. Greenard was then placed on the physically unable to perform list in July after suffering a pec strain while lifting before camp. While Greenard is trying to get back healthy, it wouldn’t be a surprise if they went out and signed Reddick for relief. articles.title: Will Brewers’ Sal Frelick return soon? Here’s Pat Murphy’s latest injury update
articles.summary: With the Milwaukee Brewers coming off the series with the Seattle Mariners and starting another with the Atlanta Braves on Friday, fans have been wondering about the injury status of right fielder Sal Frelick. As the Brewers look ahead to the playoffs, the team will want to be as healthy as possi
articles._body: With the Milwaukee Brewers coming off the series with the Seattle Mariners and starting another with the Atlanta Braves on Friday, fans have been wondering about the injury status of right fielder Sal Frelick. As the Brewers look ahead to the playoffs , the team will want to be as healthy as possible, with manager Pat Murphy giving a key update on Frelick. According to Adam McCalvy of MLB.com, Frelick is not coming back to the Milwaukee team on Friday or Saturday, though Murphy teased that his return is coming very soon , as he’s still on the 10-day injured list with a shoulder injury. “Sal Frelick will not rejoin the Brewers today, nor tomorrow, Pat Murphy said. But ‘I think you’ll see him very soon,’ Murph said,” McCalvy wrote on X, formerly Twitter. This could be confusing for a lot of fans since Murphy said this before Frelick’s two rehab games on Wednesday and Thursday that they will “make a decision” on Friday of the best course of action. “Sal’s going to play [on Wednesday] night and see if his throws and his arm respond the way [they] did this past time he played,” Murphy said, via MLB.com. “Then he’s going to play another game after that to see if it responds. Back-to-back nights, if his arm can respond. If so, we can make a decision on Friday.” So far this season, Frelick has recorded a .236 batting average to go along with four home runs and 34 RBIs in 90 games and 276 at-bats, as the 26-year-old hasn’t played since July 17, when the Brewers beat the Miami Marlins in 10 innings, 2-1. At any rate, it remains to be seen when Frelick returns to the roster. The post Will Brewers’ Sal Frelick return soon? Here’s Pat Murphy’s latest injury update appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Why Flood of NBA Team Sales Isn’t Slowing
articles.summary: Bruce Kluckhohn-Imagn Images
articles._body: Friday’s shocking deal to sell the Timberwolves represents the latest in a string of NBA team sales in recent years. The moves have come as franchise valuations skyrocket and a new class of wealthy investors enters the market. There have now been 25 change-of-control sales since 2010 ; the Hornets, Bucks, Lakers, and Timberwolves were each sold twice during that period. Just since 2020, there have been 11 change-of-control sales with a combined value of $54.1 billion. One reason for the spate may simply be that the league is in a “period of rapid transition in prices, so there is a lot of uncertainty,” according to Holy Cross sports economist Victor Matheson. “If we were in a world where everyone just ‘knew’ that a fair price for an NBA franchise was, say, $5 billion, no one really ever feels like they were ripped off or got taken advantage of,” he tells Front Office Sports . “The large number of sales may not be due to some sort of dissatisfaction with your situation, but rather just that the high price makes it hard not to cash out.” There are some other common factors that explain why there have been so many team sales, but experts say there’s no single force driving the market. The Timberwolves sale is happening—at least in part—because Marc Lore wants to focus his energy on taking his food-distribution business Wonder public, a source tells FOS . The Trail Blazers were put on the market because the late Microsoft cofounder Paul Allen mandated the sale of his sports holdings before he died in 2018. Last year, Mark Walter made the Buss family an offer it couldn’t refuse , and this year Walter is selling the Lakers to raise cash while the loans underpinning his business empire are under federal investigation . “There are independent reasons for all of them,” one legal industry source who has worked on NBA team sales tells FOS . Still, there is a through line on the other side of these transactions: Buyers aren’t lifelong fans of the franchise, local businesspeople, or even residents of the markets they are buying into. They are investors looking at sports franchises as increasingly valuable, and sophisticated, financial assets. Marc Stad, who became a limited partner in the Timberwolves when Lore and Alex Rodriguez bought the team, is now taking control of the franchise. He built his fortune in Silicon Valley through his firm, Dragoneer Investment Group. Tom Dundon, who bought the Blazers last summer, lives in Dallas. He also owns the NHL’s Hurricanes, who play their home games roughly 3,000 miles away from the Blazers. Bob Iger, who with Joshua Kushner is purchasing the Lakers, grew up a Knicks fan and has been quoted as saying he “ couldn’t root for the Lakers very easily .” Kushner lives in New York . “In the past, what I would see is that people who wanted these teams and won the bids were people who loved the team,” says an investment banker who advises on both change-of-control and minority stake sales in pro sports. “They had made money, their favorite team came on the market, and bang, they were in. That trend is moving away. There doesn’t seem to be as much affinity for the teams people buy now. That’s probably not a good thing in the long run for the fans.” That’s because the interest of the local fan base may not always align with the pursuit of returns. Dundon, for example, has already caused fans in Portland to worry about whether he might try to move the team as he fights over whether he should put any of his own money into upgrades to the Moda Center . The shift is partly a reflection of how much the underlying assets, NBA teams, have changed. And the evolution is significant: In 2014, Wesley Edens and Marc Lasry bought the Bucks at a $550 million valuation; in 2023, Lasry sold his piece of the team in a deal valuing the Bucks at $3.5 billion. Jesse Silvertown, principal at forensic accounting firm Hesperus, told FOS last year that the NBA is “the most investor-friendly league in North American pro sports,” thanks to a higher cap on private capital owning stakes in teams, limited labor strife, and a big-money, long-term media-rights deal . Sports was once thought of as a family business, with teams as prized loss-leaders in broader portfolios. The vestiges of that era lasted until somewhat recently; a legal industry source told FOS of working on an NBA sale just over a decade ago and finding that the organization was still cutting some paychecks by hand. (The team was purchased for less than $400 million, a pittance in the modern NBA.) The growth of private equity, as well as booms in tech and artificial intelligence, have created a new class of prospective sports owners that view teams through the same lens they view the rest of their portfolio. For a tech investor whose wealth is concentrated in one industry, a sports franchise can offer diversification into an asset whose value is driven by different factors, including media rights, league economics, and scarcity. With NBA team values rising so rapidly, that diversification can come with the potential for significant financial returns. “Part of what’s happened, especially with private equity moving into sports, is that people treat sports more like a business investment than a passion investment,” the investment-banking industry source says. “So, you’re getting people that own these things who don’t really love the team. They love the returns.” The post Why Flood of NBA Team Sales Isn’t Slowing appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Los Lobos Settles Sony Music Lawsuit Over ‘Desperado’ Movie Soundtrack Royalties
articles.summary: The Chicano rock band is still suing a different Sony subsidiary over the La Bamba film soundtrack.
articles._body: Los Lobos has reached a settlement with Sony Music Entertainment over royalties for “Canción del Mariachi,” the Chicano rock band’s collaboration with Antonio Banderas from the 1995 western Desperado . A Friday (Aug. 21) court filing, obtained and first reported by Billboard , states that Los Lobos and Sony Music have jointly agreed to dismiss the band’s breach of contract lawsuit . An attorney for Los Lobos, Evan Cohen , told Billboard that the matter has been settled but declined to share any deal terms. A Sony rep did not immediately return a request for comment. Related Los Lobos Sues Sony Over Song Royalties From ‘La Bamba,’ ‘Desperado’ Movie Soundtracks: ‘Egregious’ HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery BE:FIRST Is Ready for the World: Inside the J-Pop Superstars' Long-Planned U.S. Breakthrough Los Lobos sued Sony Music, whose imprint Milan Records handles distribution for “Canción del Mariachi,” in December 2025. The band claimed it hadn’t received any digital royalties for the recording, even though streams have skyrocketed since mixed martial artist Ilia “El Matador” Topuria made it his walkout anthem in recent years. “Despite the specific knowledge that the popularity of the recording was spiking and reaching new audiences, Sony and Milan still paid nothing to Los Lobos for streaming, and continues to pay nothing, for streaming anywhere in the world or for any time period,” read the lawsuit. Sony Music broadly denied wrongdoing and liability in its first response to the lawsuit in February. Banderas was not involved in the case. Even after Friday’s settlement, Los Lobos is not entirely done fighting against the Sony corporation. The band still has another lawsuit pending against a different division of the Japanese media conglomerate, Sony Pictures Entertainment, over royalties from the 1987 Ritchie Valens biopic La Bamba . That case, filed in November 2025, alleges that Los Lobos has been deprived of international streaming royalties for various Valens covers that the band recorded for the La Bamba soundtrack. This includes Los Lobos’ version of “La Bamba,” which spent three weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1987. Sony Pictures and its subsidiary studio, Columbia Pictures, are in charge of royalty accounting for that soundtrack outside the U.S. and Canada. Sony Pictures claims it has complied with all payment obligations to Los Lobos. According to court filings, the company investigated after the La Bamba lawsuit was filed and realized that $17,000 worth of foreign streaming royalties had been underpaid for a “discrete time period.” Lawyers for Sony Pictures say the company promptly sent that amount to the band, plus interest, for a total of $22,000 this past January. But Los Lobos says more money is still owed, and mediation remains ongoing.

articles.title: How Klay Thompson is perfect Heat teammate for Giannis, Bam Adebayo
articles.summary: With the Miami Heat preparing for the 2026-27 season, the team is not done making moves after the blockbuster trade for superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo, as the franchise is on its way to acquiring another big piece. As the expectation is that Klay Thompson will sign with the Heat after being boug
articles._body: With the Miami Heat preparing for the 2026-27 season , the team is not done making moves after the blockbuster trade for superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo, as the franchise is on its way to acquiring another big piece. As the expectation is that Klay Thompson will sign with the Heat after being bought out by the Dallas Mavericks, the acquisition will be a major turning point for the organization. Thompson was to be owed $17.5 million next season, but Dallas and the player “navigated a buyout,” according to ESPN’s Shams Charania, as one of the all-time greatest shooters signaled that he “wanted to play for a contender.” This line of thinking tracks, as Thompson said publicly on a Twitch livestream with user “PlaqueBoyMax” that he wanted to “compete for a championship.” “I want to compete for a championship. Not necessarily win another one, but have the chance to go and try and get another one,” Thompson said on Aug. 13. “I want to play a role on a team that can make a deep playoff run, whether it’s this season or next season. That’s really my only goal.” Mavericks G/F Klay Thompson says that he wants to compete for a championship, not necessarily win one, but have the chance to compete and try and win a title and play a role on a team that can make a deep playoff run #MFFL ( : @PlaqueBoyMax Twitch) pic.twitter.com/gEpG18RDhi — Kevin Gray Jr. (@KevinGraySports) August 14, 2026 The Heat’s top priority after LeBron James signed with the Philadelphia 76ers, where the team was one of the finalists, was to get the four-time NBA champion. This time, the waiting game paid off, and Thompson will seemingly be on his way to take his talents to South Beach, but how will the fit be? Spoiler alert, it’ll be near-perfect. Here’s why: Will Klay Thompson be the next Ray Allen for the Heat? While the Heat ended up signing Tim Hardaway Jr., who shot 40.7 percent from three-point range on 6.9 attempts from deep per game, the team was still in need of more spacing and shooting on the team. It was easy to see why Miami had vast interest in a player like Thompson, who is without a doubt one of the best shooters the game has ever seen. Though 36 years old, Thompson is still very much capable of being an elite catch-and-shoot option for the Heat, especially with the top scoring options on the team being Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo, who will command attention low. There could be a ton of opportunities coming in the way of Thompson, whose workload and fit with the Mavericks have gone down. One major comparison that could excite Miami fans is that Thompson could be having the same role as Ray Allen had with the Heat during his iconic time with the team from 2012 to 2014. Everyone remembers Allen’s legendary game-tying three-point shot in Game 6 of the 2013 NBA Finals, as he was 37 years old when it happened, and while his role had been decreased compared to earlier in his career, he was still integral to the team. Thompson could easily follow in the same footsteps, as while he won’t be utilized the way he was early with the Golden State Warriors, the guard will still be a vital piece in what Pat Riley, Erik Spoelstra, and Miami hope is another championship run. How financially it’ll work for the Heat and Klay Thompson The Heat likely see the same vision, which is why Thompson was made a top target for the team after playing the waiting game on James. According to ClutchPoints’ NBA insider Brett Siegel, the likelihood is that the Heat will be using the remaining $8.9 million in the mid-level exception. “Throughout the offseason, the Mavs had pushed back at the idea of buying Thompson out of his contract, making it clear to rival teams that they intended to trade the five-time All-Star. The Heat have long held interest in Thompson, but only by way of a buyout, where they would then be able to offer him their remaining $8.9 million mid-level exception,” Siegel wrote on Friday. “Thompson instantly became the organization’s top target, which is why they did not make an offer using their MLE to Bradley Beal or DeMar DeRozan, two other veteran free agents linked to Miami,” Siegel continued. “The Heat have about $10.6 million to work with before reaching their first-apron hard cap.” As Bradley Beal decided to return to the Los Angeles Clippers, and with the domino of Thompson expecting to sign with the Heat, another team target was DeMar DeRozan, who ended up signing with the Denver Nuggets. Klay Thompson’s outlook with the Heat Looking at Thompson’s time with the Dallas Mavericks, his time with the team was an unusual one, to say the least, as he was considered one of the missing pieces after the team made the NBA Finals led by Luka Doncic and Kyrie Irving. However, one of the most shocking trades in NBA history happened before that season’s trade deadline, when Doncic was dealt to the Los Angeles Lakers. As Thompson was caught in the middle of an organizational shift, it’s no wonder he intended to go to a contender, leading to the buyout, which was helpful since there was some talk of Dallas trading the veteran. Last season with Dallas, Thompson averaged 11.7 points, 3.4 renounds, and 2.2 assists per game while shooting 44.8 percent from the field and 38.3 percent from deep, which is the lowest in his career, taking 7.6 attempts per game from that range. It’s easy to expect an uptick in points and attempts, as Thompson’s talents were desperately needed on the Heat next to Antetokounmpo and Adebayo. A projected starting lineup of Thompson, Antetokounmpo, Adebayo, Davion Mitchell, and Andrew Wiggins is sure to excite fans heading into the season, as Miami is entering a new chapter of its franchise. articles.title: Texas Tech QBs Kirk Francis and Lloyd Jones Embrace Competition, Prepare for Their Opportunity
articles.summary: Redraidersports.com was on site for the media availability after practice #12 on Wednesday. Here is what Kirk Francis and Lloyd Jones had to say about how fall camp is going and the competition battles going on in camp.
articles._body: Texas Tech’s quarterback room is taking shape as fall camp continues, with transfer Kirk Francis and Lloyd Jones both making the most of their opportunities. Francis has embraced the leadership and preparation that come with being a veteran backup, while Jones continues to build confidence after his ACL recovery. With both quarterbacks competing for the QB2 role, the pair is pushing each other while adjusting to Mack Leftwich’s offense and preparing for the opportunity to step onto the field when their number is called. Texas Tech’s quarterback-friendly offense gives Kirk Francis freedom at the line of scrimmage Texas Tech transfer quarterback Kirk Francis, who arrived from Tulsa to provide valuable depth to the position room, says Coach Mack Leftwich’s offense is quarterback-friendly and gives him plenty of freedom at the line of scrimmage. Francis added that the biggest adjustment so far has been the level of talent surrounding him. “Yeah, you know, I think the biggest adjustment’s definitely just been the talent around us. I think he’s a pretty quarterback-friendly offense. He lets us play in, and, you know, he gives us a lot of freedom at the line of scrimmage to change things, get into better looks. But I think he does a really good job of coaching and teaching the offense like it’s supposed to be running. At the end of the day, he just wants us to throw completions.” Playing clean is key to success Texas Tech held its first scrimmage this past Saturday, and quarterback Kirk Francis said the offensive emphasis is simple: don’t beat yourself. Francis believes the Red Raiders can compete with anyone in the country if they eliminate self-inflicted mistakes, with pre-snap penalties remaining a major area of focus for the offense. “Yeah, I think we had a really good—we did a really good job coming out early, starting hot. That’s something that we’re really emphasizing this season. I think we can do a better job. Pre-snap penalties, play number one on the rule number one on the plan to win is not beat ourselves. At the end of the day, we think we can beat everyone we play as long as we don’t beat ourselves.” Coach McGuire’s passion sold Francis on Texas Tech Coach Joey McGuire’s passion for Texas Tech and the Lubbock community immediately stood out to Francis during his visit, making his decision a no-brainer. The support from the fans further showed him what the university means to its community. Although Francis knew he wouldn’t enter the season as the starting quarterback, he believed Texas Tech was the best place for him, embracing the opportunity to bring experience to the room and be one play away from stepping onto the field. “Yeah, I think that’s a really good question, and really, what it came down to was the people. You know, sitting in Coach McGuire’s office with my parents on my visit, you know, it was a no-brainer. Once you hear him talk, you see how passionate he is about this place and just about Lubbock and Texas Tech and the people here. It was a no-brainer. The market for me and the portal really was a bunch of G5 opportunities to come in and compete, and then a bunch of places like Texas Tech, you know, bigger brand names to come in as the two, be a guy with experience, a veteran. But honestly, you know, being one play away at a school like this, you know, which should be a top-10 ranked team in the nation preseason, you know, you can’t beat that opportunity. And playing for a guy like Coach McGuire and Coach Leftwich is something I couldn’t pass up.” Kirk Francis prepares like he’s the starter, regardless of his role Kirk Francis came to Tech knowing he was going to be the backup. He has treated his preparation no differently than if he is going to start. When Sorsby was here, Francis was slated to be QB3 now with Sorsby gone he is backing up Will Hammond. “I think it’s really no different. You know where you are on the lineup and the roster. I think that every day you’ve got to prepare like you are the guy, no matter if you are or not. And that’s kind of how I’ve approached my entire career. You know, I started as a walk-on at Tulsa. You know, started as the seventh string, and then ultimately ended up starting four games my true freshman year. And I think that that kind of mentality is what you have to have. You’ve got to expect to play.” Kirk Francis used under-recruitment as motivation Despite a productive high school career, Texas Tech quarterback Kirk Francis said it was frustrating to receive limited recruiting interest. With mostly preferred walk-on opportunities available, Francis focused on finding a program where he could see a path to the field and ultimately chose Tulsa, where his career began to take shape. “Definitely was frustrating. You know, I had a bunch of PWO opportunities at, you know, local schools, regional schools, and I think that for me it was just, where can I get on the field? Where do I see myself fitting in on an offense and in a program? And ultimately, Tulsa was that option for me, and, you know, it worked out that way.” Standouts in Francis’s eyes Kirk tells us who has been standing out to him during fall camp. Kirk mentions a player that is going to surprise some people this year. “Man, I mean, there’s so many. I don’t know if you really can pick one. I think, you know, J’Koby Williams out of the backfield, Jalen Jones and Coy Eakin in the slot, but, you know, you probably got to say Micah Hudson . You know, he’s such a big unknown for people this year, but I think they’re going to be really surprised.” West Virginia game gave Lloyd Jones belief in his ability Lloyd Jones entered the final game of last season as Texas Tech looked to protect Behren Morton , but after Mitch Griffs suffered an injury, Jones’ number was called. He delivered with several big plays, including two touchdown passes to wide receiver Micah Hudson, giving him a major confidence boost and proving to himself that he could perform on a big stage.

articles.summary: More reinforcements could be on the way for the LSU Tigers, heading into year one of Will Wade‘s second tenure with the program. Just days after landing a commitment from former UCLA guard Skyy Clark, another former Bruin could potentially be on their way to Baton Rouge. Per Field of 68’
articles._body: More reinforcements could be on the way for the LSU Tigers , heading into year one of Will Wade ‘s second tenure with the program. Just days after landing a commitment from former UCLA guard Skyy Clark , another former Bruin could potentially be on their way to Baton Rouge. Per Field of 68’s Jeff Goodman , ‘ LSU has been extremely aggressive in its pursuit of former UCLA point guard Donovan Dent since he got a TRO in California.’ Per Goodman, LSU is seen as the ‘frontrunners’ for the former Mountain West Player of the Year. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Dent previously retired from basketball earlier this year after choosing not to enter the NBA Draft. After receiving the TRO, however, one more season of ball looks to be on the table for the Riverside, Cali. native. “It’s nothing new to me, I already knew where I was at mentally,” Dent said after initially retiring. “It was a long talk with my family after the season. I wanted to make sure they understood my side of it and that they supported me through it. Once they did, it was really easy for me to adjust to it.” Dent could re-unite with former teammate Skyy Clark in Baton Rouge Across his four-year career, Dent boasts career averages of 13.4 points, 5.5 assists, and 2.5 rebounds. He was an Honorable Mention All-American in 2025, along with earning Mountain West Player of the Year and First Team All-Mountain West honors. Three of his four seasons of play came at New Mexico (2022-25), prior to spending this past season at UCLA . As of this moment, LSU currently boasts 11 players on its roster. Five of these players ( RJ Luis , Saliou Niang , Brice Dessert , Michael Ruzic , and Marcio Santos ) are still waiting to be declared eligible, however. LSU ‘s eligible players, at the moment, include Kansas State transfer guard Abdi Bashir Jr. , freshman forward Jordan Bender , UCLA transfer guard Skyy Clark , Kentucky transfer forward Mo Dioubate , UTSA transfer guard Austin Nunez , and Michigan State transfer guard Divine Ugochukwu . Will Wade regains control of the LSU Basketball program this season following a four-year absence. In that span, Wade spent two seasons at McNeese (2023-25) and last season at NC State . Across his prior five-year stint at LSU (2017-22), Wade led the Tigers to a 105-51 record and three NCAA Tournament appearances.

articles.title: Eagles waive promising WR with injury designation
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles have had some makeover in their wide receiver room this offseason, and they’ll be looking to make an impact when the season begins. Unfortunately, Johnny Wilson will not be a part of that group, as he was recently waived with an injury designation. “We signed C
articles._body: The Philadelphia Eagles have had some makeover in their wide receiver room this offseason, and they’ll be looking to make an impact when the season begins. Unfortunately, Johnny Wilson will not be a part of that group, as he was recently waived with an injury designation. “We signed C Zeke Correll and WR Brandon Hayes. We also placed Tariq Castro-Fields on the Injured Reserve List and waived/injured WR Johnny Wilson,” the team wrote on X, formerly Twitter. The Eagles selected Wilson in the sixth round of the 2024 draft out of Florida State. He appeared in 16 games in his rookie season, and he finished with five catches, 38 yards and one touchdown. Where Wilson was able to make an impact on the field was in his blocking, which helped in the running game. He was then injured last season in training camp and had to undergo surgery, which held him back from competing. It was going to be hard for him to get playing time coming back this season, as they added receivers such as Hollywood Brown in free agency and drafted Makai Lemon in the first round. In a corresponding move, it looks like the Eagles were able to sign Brandon Hayes, and it’ll be interesting to see what his role looks like on the team. As for Wilson, he’ll be going through waivers, and there’s a chance that a team claims him. The Eagles recently took part in joint practice with the New England Patriots over the past few days, and the offense had some highs and lows. Jalen Hurts threw several picks over the two days, and it looks like he’s still getting acclimated to the offensive system that Sean Mannion has put in place. This is the time for the Eagles to work out the bad plays, and things should be better when the season begins. articles.title: Carolina Basketball Announces 2026-27 Roster
articles.summary: North Carolina’s 16-man roster features five returners and 11 newcomers, including six transfers and five freshmen.
articles._body: CHAPEL HILL, N.C. — North Carolina’s 2026-27 roster is officially set. The program unveiled its complete 16-man roster for Michael Malone’s first season in Chapel Hill, featuring 11 new faces. The Tar Heels return just five players from last season’s team, with Malone’s inaugural roster consisting of four freshmen, six college transfers and one international addition. Seniors Jarin Stevenson, Jaydon Young and Evan Smith, junior John Holbrook and sophomore Isaiah Denis make up UNC’s returning contingent. Malone supplemented that group with six transfers from across college basketball: graduate students Angelo Brizzi (Buffalo) and Cameron Fens (South Dakota), senior Terrence Brown (Utah), and sophomores Matt Able (NC State), Neo Avdalas (Virginia Tech) and Cade Bennerman, who redshirted last season at Northwestern. Alexandros Samodurov joins the Tar Heels as a junior after playing professionally for Panathinaikos in Athens, Greece. UNC’s four freshmen are Maximo Adams (Los Angeles), Sayon Keita (Mali), Malloy Smith (Encino, Calif.) and Kevin Thomas (Fort Lauderdale, Fla.). Keita arrives in Chapel Hill after playing at the U18 level for FC Barcelona in Spain. Avdalas and Samodurov are the first Greek players in program history, while Keita becomes the second Tar Heel from Africa, joining Senegal native Makhtar Ndiaye, who played at UNC from 1996-98. Their additions bring the program’s all-time total of international players to 18. 2026-27 UNC Men’s Basketball Roster  1 – Terrence Brown, Sr., 6-3 180 (Minneapolis, Minn.) 2 – Isaiah Denis, So., 6-4 185 (Charlotte, N.C.) 3 – Matt Able, So., 6-5 200 (Baltimore, Md.) 4 – Jaydon Young, Sr., 6-4 200 (Goldsboro, N.C.) 5 – Kevin Thomas, Fr., 6-6 205 (Fort Lauderdale, Fla.) 14 – Angelo Brizzi, Gr., 6-3 200 (Warrenton, Va.) 15 – Jarin Stevenson, Sr., 6-10 220 (Chapel Hill, N.C.) 17 – Neoklis Avdalas, So., 6-9 220 (Athens, Greece) 21 – Sayon Keita, Fr., 7-1 205 (Bamako, Mali) 22 – Alexandros Samodurov, Jr., 6-11 225 (Evosmos, Greece) 25 – Maximo Adams, Fr., 6-7 220 (Los Angeles, Calif.) 30 – Malloy Smith, Fr., 6-5 180 (Encino, Calif.) 32 – Evan Smith, Sr., 6-1 200 (Charlotte, N.C.) 35 – Cade Bennerman, So., 7-0 205 (Nashville, Tenn.) 54 – Cameron Fens, Gr., 7-0 255 (Dubuque, Iowa) 99 – John Holbrook, Jr., 6-8 230 (Hickory, N.C.)

articles.title: Sources: Nuggets to sign DeMar DeRozan after trading Peyton Watson
articles.summary: The Denver Nuggets are signing six-time NBA All-Star DeMar DeRozan to a minimum contract for the 2026-27 NBA season, league sources told ClutchPoints on Friday afternoon. DeRozan, 37, has been available as an unrestricted free agent since the Sacramento Kings waived him in July to create financia
articles._body: The Denver Nuggets are signing six-time NBA All-Star DeMar DeRozan to a minimum contract for the 2026-27 NBA season, league sources told ClutchPoints on Friday afternoon. DeRozan, 37, has been available as an unrestricted free agent since the Sacramento Kings waived him in July to create financial flexibility. Only $10 million of DeRozan’s 25.7 million contract with the Kings for the upcoming year was guaranteed this offseason, which is why the Kings decided to part ways with him. Less than two days after agreeing to a sign-and-trade with Peyton Watson and the Cleveland Cavaliers , the Nuggets land DeRozan as a key secondary star and scorer alongside Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray. Throughout his entire career, DeRozan has been known for being a reliable scoring option who has always been readily available. This past year, he played in 77 games, averaging 18.4 points, 2.9 rebounds, and 4.1 assists per game with the Kings while shooting 49.7 percent from the floor. The 2025-26 season was the first time since the 2012-13 season that DeRozan failed to average more than 20 points per game. Over the last five seasons, DeRozan has played at least 74 games every season. He ranks 18th on the NBA’s all-time scoring list and is fourth among active players, trailing only LeBron James, Kevin Durant, and James Harden. Since the Sacramento Kings waived him, multiple teams have expressed interest in signing DeRozan. There was a lot of noise initially about a potential reunion with the Toronto Raptors, but the attention for DeRozan quickly shifted to Denver, Miami, and Washington. After recently parting ways with Watson by way of his sign-and-trade, ClutchPoints reported on Wednesday night that the Nuggets were determined to land DeRozan on a minimum deal. Although initial word surrounding the veteran upon being bought out by the Kings was that he did not want to take a minimum deal, he ultimately settles for this spot in Denver, a championship contender in the West. The Heat were also linked to DeRozan since he was waived by the Kings, but Miami opted to wait and pursue Klay Thompson. Upon being bought out by the Dallas Mavericks on Friday, news of Thompson intending to sign with the Heat emerged. Whether or not DeRozan starts in Denver is the big question at hand. If he does slide into the Nuggets’ starting lineup, he would start over Christian Braun, who started in all 44 games he appeared in during the 2025-26 regular season. DeRozan has likely accepted a bench role with the Nuggets, where he will be the team’s reliable sixth man and go-to scoring option when Murray or Jokic check out of the game. Last season, the Nuggets went 54-28 before losing in the first round of the playoffs to Anthony Edwards and the Minnesota Timberwolves. With Jokic again declining to take an extension this offseason and their core getting older, the Nuggets are doing everything they can to maximize their championship potential. That is why signing DeRozan and bringing him off the bench is a major win in what has been a quiet offseason for Denver.
