articles.title: Cardinals’ Alec Burleson explains why he didn’t want to be traded before deadline
articles.summary: Even if the St. Louis Cardinals (66-63) do not grab the final National League Wild Card slot this season, their future looks quite bright. But the skies above Busch Stadium would probably be much dimmer if the organization had shipped out Alec Burleson ahead of the MLB trade deadline. The star fi
articles._body: Even if the St. Louis Cardinals (66-63) do not grab the final National League Wild Card slot this season, their future looks quite bright. But the skies above Busch Stadium would probably be much dimmer if the organization had shipped out Alec Burleson ahead of the MLB trade deadline. The star first baseman is proud of what he has helped the franchise accomplish in 2026, and he does not want to miss out on the next phase of this Redbirds rebirth. “Obviously, we’re building toward something that is gonna look really good in the next couple years, and I would like to think I’ve been a small part of that,” Burleson told the “Foul Territory” podcast on Friday. “On the off chance {that I was traded at the deadline}, it would have kind of hurt a little bit. Just to leave that, and leave what little bit I’ve contributed to what it’s gonna look like in the next few years.” The Cardinals dealt outfielder Lars Nootbaar , right-handed starting pitcher Dustin May and left-handed reliever JoJo Romero, but they opted to keep Burleson . It is easy to see why. "On the off chance that I was traded at the deadline, it would've hurt." @AlecBurleson9 wants to see it through with the Cardinals. pic.twitter.com/xURZs2Quop — Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) August 21, 2026 The 2025 Silver Slugger Award winner is a complete hitter and does not reach the open market until after the 2028 campaign. In the midst of a stellar August, he is batting .288 with 21 homers, 93 RBIs, a .355 on-base percentage, .489 slugging percentage, .844 OPS and MLB-leading 33 doubles this season. Alec Burleson is a beloved franchise building block whom fans want to see in a Cardinals uniform for many years to come. He reciprocates their adulation. “I love St. Louis, the fans, the staff and the players… it’s very comfortable, feels like home,” the North Carolina native said. “I’m not sure what it’s gonna look like in the next few years, but I would definitely like to be around for it and contribute to a lot of winning baseball in St. Louis.” Fresh off their most bonkers win of the season , Burleson and the Cards will begin a crucial road series versus the Philadelphia Phillies (70-58) on Friday night. First pitch is scheduled for 6:40 p.m. ET. The post Cardinals’ Alec Burleson explains why he didn’t want to be traded before deadline appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Thunder + fiber-optic cabling used for seismic imaging
articles.summary: Thunderstorms make seismic waves that can be used to find sub-surface features.
articles._body: Most of what we know about the Earth's interior comes from observing seismic waves. These travel at somewhat different speeds depending on the details of the rock they're moving through—whether it's solid or semi-molten, how much water is present, whether it's fractured or solid material, and so on. Get enough data from enough seismic events, and you can start piecing together a picture of what's present at different depths below the surface. In many cases, we can get this data from naturally occurring events like earthquakes. In others, we intentionally create waves using things like explosives, providing the opportunity to do imaging in specific areas without needing to wait for an earthquake. Now, a team of scientists at Penn State suggests there's a potential option that sits between waiting for an earthquake and triggering your own seismic event: thunderstorms. Some of the energy carried by thunder enters the Earth's upper crust, triggering what are termed "thunderquakes." But, for various physical reasons, the seismic signals are extremely complex, making it difficult to extract clear signals from them. The Penn State team says it has finally constructed a model that can help make sense of this complexity and used it to reconstruct the terrain under the local campus. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Show HN: Zroar – Serialized Roaring Bitmaps in Zig
articles.summary: zroar is a ground-up implementation of Roaring Bitmaps data structure in Zig. zroar stores both the keys and (array, bitmap) containers in a single flat byte buffer, making the in-memory representation equal to the on-disk or over-the-network representation, eliminating the serialization/deserial
articles._body: zroar is a ground-up implementation of Roaring Bitmaps data structure in Zig. zroar stores both the keys and (array, bitmap) containers in a single flat byte buffer, making the in-memory representation equal to the on-disk or over-the-network representation, eliminating the serialization/deserialization step entirely. The design was originally aimed at systems which keep their posting lists on disk, but zroar performs faster than CRoaring even for purely in-memory ops, due to CPU cache locality. Against CRoaring 5.0's benchmarking suite (ported to Zig), zroar is faster in 339 out of 360 tests, being 2x-9x faster (geometric mean), and up to 600x faster on serialize/deserialize. zroar avoids complex mechanism (like adaptive radix trees), uses Zig native SIMD ops and is simpler. The main logic is written in ~2000 lines of code, while CRoaring's 64-bit bitmap codebase is over 17000 LOC. Not yet: By choice, zroar doesn't support run containers, and is 64-bit only. There are more details in the GitHub README. Try it out! I'd love feedback on the API and design. zroar is a Zig-based successor to my other project, sroar in Go, which showed a similar boost. So, I think this design should show performance gains in any language. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49393285 Points: 3 # Comments: 0

articles.title: Legendary Investor Ray Dalio Touts Bitcoin — With Gold — To Hedge Against Incoming Debt Crisis
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Legendary Investor Ray Dalio Touts Bitcoin — With Gold — To Hedge Against Incoming Debt Crisis Top investor Ray Dalio has again sung Bitcoin’s praises. But only a little bit.  The billionaire hedge fund boss said in his latest essay that he expected  “non-government-produced monies like gold and bitcoin to do relatively well” as government debt grows.  Dalio, who founded one of the world’s largest hedge funds, Bridgewater Associates, has long warned investors about the size of America’s debt. U.S. national debt passed the $40 trillion mark this week.  JUST IN: Billionaire Ray Dalio suggests diversifying into gold, bonds, "and a bit of Bitcoin." pic.twitter.com/Z0TCviiTBV — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) August 21, 2026 “As general advice, I suggest diversifying well in asset classes and countries that have strong income statements and balance sheets and are not having great internal political and external geopolitical conflicts, underweighting debt assets like bonds, and overweighting gold and a bit of Bitcoin,” Dalio wrote.  He added that major economies like the U.K., U.S., Europe, and Japan all have similar debt and deficit problems and therefore assets like bitcoin — which are not issued by governments — could end up benefiting.  Dalio has gone from saying he wouldn’t invest in Bitcoin over the years to finally admitting it was in his portfolio.  Last year, Dalio said that bitcoin only made up 1% of his investments. He reiterated that point this year, and warned that although no one can print more bitcoin, it can be hurt by quantum computing advances.  Back in 2020, the billionaire investor said that the cryptocurrency was too volatile to use as money but that it was worth holding a little bit. Gold, on the other hand, should be held by all investors, he added.  Dalio’s latest essay explains that when governments over-borrow and central banks respond by printing money to cover the gap between debt supply and demand, the value of the currency gets debased. Bitcoiners have long argued that the oldest cryptocurrency can work as a hedge against government printing, just like gold.  And Bitcoin has in the past benefited from governments expanding their money supplies.  This post Legendary Investor Ray Dalio Touts Bitcoin — With Gold — To Hedge Against Incoming Debt Crisis first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .

articles.title: Phoebe Bridgers Earns Her First Billboard Airplay No. 1 With ‘Lost Boys’
articles.summary: The lead single from Lost Weekend tops the Adult Alternative Airplay chart.
articles._body: Phoebe Bridger s tops a Billboard airplay chart for the first time as a solo artist, ruling the Aug. 29-dated Adult Alternative Airplay survey with “Lost Boys.” The song rises 2-1 in its eighth week on the ranking, following the Aug. 14 release of parent album Lost Weekend . Bridgers first reached Adult Alternative Airplay in 2017 with “Motion Sickness,” which rose to No. 26 in early 2018. Prior to “Lost Boys,” she logged her best peak with “Sidelines,” which hit No. 12 in 2022. Bridgers does, however, have previous No. 1 success on Adult Alternative Airplay. Boygenius , her group with Julien Baker and Lucy Dacus , led for seven weeks in 2023 with “Not Strong Enough”; follow-up “Cool About It” reached No. 2. “Lost Boys” makes Bridgers the second act to hit No. 1 on Adult Alternative Airplay for the first time in 2026, following Chris Stapleton , whose duet with Mumford & Sons , “Here,” led for two weeks in July. She’s the first first-timer to do so without any other acts since St. Paul & the Broken Bones reigned with “Sushi and Coca-Cola” in October. Concurrently, “Lost Boys” lifts 23-22 on Alternative Airplay ; her previous best, “Kyoto,” peaked at No. 25 in 2021 (boygenius’ “Not Strong Enough” hit No. 11). On the all-rock-format, audience-based Rock & Alternative Airplay chart, “Lost Boys” climbs 21-17 with 2.2 million audience impressions, up 13%, in the week ending Aug. 20, according to Luminate. “Lost Boys” is the lead single from Lost Weekend , Bridgers’ third studio album, which is set to impact the latest Billboard album charts. All lists dated Aug. 29 will update on Billboard.com on Tuesday, Aug. 25, with the top 10 of the Billboard 200 to be revealed Sunday, Aug. 23.

articles.title: WNBA Tanking Season Is Officially Underway for Several Teams
articles.summary: Colin Hubbard-Imagn Images
articles._body: The WNBA’s eight playoff teams have been pretty clear for the last several weeks. That appears to have activated the tank signal for teams on the other end of the standings. With less than 10 games remaining for each WNBA team as of Friday, the gap between the Dallas Wings (21–16) and the Portland Fire (15–20) for the final playoff spot is five games. The Toronto Tempo, once a threat to make the playoffs, have lost 12 consecutive games, with their last win coming against the New York Liberty on July 12—which was 40 days ago. The expansion franchise has been hammered by injuries all season; notably, max player Brittney Sykes and rookie Kiki Rice have missed a combined 34 games. While both players have returned in recent weeks, on Wednesday against the Mystics, Sykes was ruled out for “left foot load management.” Marina Mabrey, the team’s other max player, also missed that game with a right hamstring injury, and she’s already been ruled out of Friday’s game as well. Toronto currently has the second-best odds to win the 2027 WNBA draft lottery , and has a few more losses from jumping past the Connecticut Sun for the best odds. The Los Angeles Sparks have not shown the same futility as the Tempo—their losing streak is currently at six. But on Thursday, coach Lynne Roberts practically admitted that the team is tanking. According to reporter John W. Davis , Roberts informed the team that bench players will receive additional playing time for the rest of the season, even though their starters are healthy. The Sparks currently have the fifth-best odds to win the lottery, and recently passed the Fire, who have won two in a row. Los Angeles also traded five-time All-Star Kelsey Plum at the trade deadline. Tanking in the WNBA is not nearly as egregious as it has been in the NBA , which recently enacted sweeping changes to address the issue . The WNBA also has a different lottery system than the NBA, taking into account a team’s standings over the last two seasons, making tanking efforts more difficult. That is why the Seattle Storm, who went 23–19 last season, have the fourth-worst lottery odds despite having the worst record in the league this season. (Because the Tempo and Fire are expansion teams, their record this season is compared to other teams based on win percentage.) There are also teams that haven’t tanked because they have no incentive to do so; in particular, the Chicago Sky and Phoenix Mercury do not own the rights to their 2027 first-round picks. The Sky traded a pick swap to the Mystics last year to acquire Ariel Atkins (who is no longer on the team), while the Mercury traded their pick to acquire Plum . And the Fire, who control their own draft pick, seem to just want to bring the winning culture to their expansion franchise. GM Vanja Černivec told Front Office Sports in June that the team wants “to be as competitive as possible.” “We definitely don’t want to start a franchise thinking about getting the number one draft pick next year,” she said. But it’s not surprising why some teams have chosen to tank. USC star JuJu Watkins is expected to be available at the top of the board for the lucky team that has the No. 1 pick in 2027. And for those who fall just short, Texas star Madison Booker and Notre Dame’s Hannah Hidalgo are also blue-chip prospects. Considering recent drafts produced immediate superstar players including Olivia Miles (2026), Paige Bueckers (2025), Caitlin Clark (2024), and Aliyah Boston (2023), teams can rightfully believe a young star can help expedite a rebuild. articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers are at a crossroads with Joey Porter Jr., as a handful of teams are being linked with the cornerback. With how things currently stand, the Blitzburgh could either offer an extension or part ways and let him enter the market. But while talking about both of these scenarios, is
articles._body: Pittsburgh Steelers are at a crossroads with Joey Porter Jr. , as a handful of teams are being linked with the cornerback. With how things currently stand, the Blitzburgh could either offer an extension or part ways and let him enter the market. But while talking about both of these scenarios, is a trade consideration even making sense for the Steelers? Would they really consider a breakup with JPJ amid a soaring CB market? Or would it be a grave mistake? “Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. is a name multiple teams around the NFL have wondered about as a potential trade target, per sources. JPJ is in the final year of his rookie contract, and with where the CB market is, teams have wondered if Pittsburgh could ultimately be open to a move with the Pro Bowl caliber corner,” NFL insider Jordan Schultz recently tweeted. Porter Jr., who has been away from NFL action due to a back injury , is said to be allegedly testing the waters. Multiple reports also mention that he is keeping his cards close to his chest while he waits for a long-term commitment offer. However, things could be tricky if he is really considering it. The California-born star is in the last year of his rookie contract. Any potential trade that the Steelers would consider could be structured around a high first-round pick in it. A couple of teams could make the cut in that case. But none of the reports have clearly mentioned that the Pittsburgh front office is entertaining any such phone calls talking about a trade. With a new coaching structure underway after Mike McCarthy’s appointment, a trade on the go looks very much on the horizon. Because if the Steelers had to commit to a long-term plan with Porter Jr., his recent run-in with an injury could have made less sense. On the other side of the conversation, his last NFL season was nothing short of what could be called a productive year. In 14 games he played for the Steelers during the 2025 NFL season, he started all of them. Additionally, his career-high 14 pass deflections also came during the same past season, while also finishing with 52 tackles and one interception. While it was considerably enticing for teams on the lookout, it is his injury status and a lack of activity that could play in favour of those enquiring to land him. However, we would still wait to see how things go and who puts the final nail in the coffin before September 13. Watch this space for all the speculation and rumors involving the Pittsburgh Steelers and Joey Porter Jr. The post Would Steelers’ Joey Porter Jr. trade be grave mistake or savvy decision as CB market explodes? appeared first on ClutchPoints .

She has spent her career building organizations, developing partnerships and bringing people together around a shared purpose. We’re excited to have her leadership as we expand the Foundation’s reach and create more opportunities for people to experience the power of music.” —  Ariel King

articles.title: Why I’m Entering the Grammys’ New Asian Pop Category Despite the Backlash (Guest Column)
articles.summary: While the controversy over the new category is understandable, we shouldn’t overlook its possibilities.
articles._body: When I first heard that people were criticizing the Recording Academy’s new Best Asian Pop Music Performance category, my honest reaction was surprise. I didn’t understand why people were upset. From where I stood, I saw an organization trying to recognize music, languages and cultures that have historically received less attention within the American music industry. Why wouldn’t we welcome that? Related Recording Academy Discussing Future of New Asian Pop Category Phoebe Bridgers, KATSEYE Bag First No. 1s In Australia 'We Know What We Want': With a New Recording Studio and Label Deal, DMA'S Are Just Getting Started Then I started reading more about the concerns, and I began to understand where some Asian artists and fans were coming from. If you have spent years fighting to have Asian artists recognized simply as pop artists, the creation of a separate category can raise an uncomfortable question: Is this opening another door for us, or building another room that people expect us to stay inside? The language requirement raises questions of its own. An artist can be Asian and create music that does not prominently use an Asian language. Does that make the music less Asian? Should language define genre or identity? Those are legitimate questions, and I still decided to enter. That choice is not because I think every detail of the new category is perfect. I don’t. I think the Recording Academy could have benefited from hearing from a wider group of Asian and non-Asian musicians while developing the rules and explaining the intention behind them. (I’m glad the Academy is doing that now .) I’m entering because I see another possibility in this category, one that I don’t want us to lose sight of while debating its shortcomings: discovery. As a Recording Academy voting member, I imagine listening to the entries and hearing artists from Japan, China, Korea and other parts of Asia whom I have never encountered before. I might discover a kind of J-pop I never knew existed or hear an independent Mandarin artist who otherwise may never have crossed my path. Even within K-pop, there are many different musical approaches that American listeners rarely encounter because our image of an entire country’s music can become defined by the few artists who achieve enormous global fame. Related BTS’ Decision to Sit Out the Grammys Brings New Attention to the Academy’s Asian Pop Category That matters, because some of the criticism surrounding the category seems to assume that it exists primarily for the Asian superstars we already know. But Asian pop is much larger than the handful of names that have broken through internationally. For an independent artist working in Mandarin, Japanese, Korean or another Asian language, this category could provide something that is extraordinarily difficult to obtain: the attention of thousands of music professionals who might otherwise never press play. At the same time, I don’t believe Asian artists should stop competing everywhere else. An Asian artist belongs in record of the year, song of the year and album of the year. Creating a place where Asian-language music can receive additional recognition should never become an argument for excluding those artists from the rest of the music world. Both things can be true. That tension feels especially personal to me because I have never thought of language as the thing that defines my music. I was born in China, but I began my professional music career in the United States. I reached the top 25 on Billboard ’s Adult Contemporary Airplay chart, yet I have recorded in Mandarin, English, Spanish, Italian and many other languages. Related Stray Kids’ Latest Becomes Milestone 25th K-pop Album to Top Billboard 200: Full List When I write, I don’t begin with nationality. I begin with emotion. Love does not become a different emotion when I sing about it in Mandarin. Heartbreak does not change because the words are Spanish. Fear, hope, loneliness and joy belong to every culture. But language still matters deeply. As a native Mandarin speaker, I know there is a difference between understanding words and feeling them. When I hear an important idea in English, I understand it, but sometimes I am translating it internally or processing exactly what it means. When I hear that same idea in Mandarin, it can reach me immediately. It goes directly to the heart. That realization is one reason I have recorded so much multilingual music. When I released “Could You Lend Me a Smile” in 16 language versions, I didn’t want people around the world simply to receive a literal translation. We worked to adapt the message so listeners could experience it naturally within their own language and culture. To me, that distinction is important. Translation tells someone what the words mean. Adaptation gives the listener a chance to feel what I felt when I wrote them. That philosophy is also why I am submitting the Chinese-English version of “It’s Too Late to Love You,” my duet with three-time Grammy winner Narada Michael Walden. Narada and I come from very different backgrounds. We grew up with different cultures, musical influences and life experiences, yet those differences have never created a barrier in the studio. If anything, they made the music richer. Narada is extraordinarily open to sounds outside his own experience. When I first brought him songs influenced by the emotional storytelling I grew up hearing in Chinese music, he did not ask me to make them sound less Chinese or more American. He heard something beautiful in the difference and encouraged it. That, to me, is what cultural exchange should look like. You don’t have to erase where you came from in order to connect with somebody from somewhere else. I have spent much of my life moving between cultures, and over time I stopped thinking of that as something I needed to resolve. articles.title: Luke Combs Claims His 21st Country Airplay No. 1 With ‘Be By You’ — Here’s Why It’s an Outlier
articles.summary: It’s the star’s third leader from his album The Way I Am.
articles._body: Luke Combs earns his 21st No. 1 on Billboard ’s Country Airplay chart as “Be By You” rises a spot on 32.8 million audience impressions, up 3%, Aug. 14-20, according to Luminate. Related Watch Luke Combs Make His Voice Acting Debut in Disney Series ‘Big City Greens’: ‘This Will Be Way Cooler in My Kids’ Eyes Than Anything Else I’ve Done’ Luke Combs Becomes First Solo Country Act to Headline Wembley Stadium Luke Combs’ ‘Sleepless’ Stays Up at No. 1 on Country Airplay Chart for Fifth Week The song becomes his third leader from his latest album, The Way I Am . “Back in the Saddle” (two weeks on top) and “Sleepless in a Hotel Room” (five) reached the summit in November and April, respectively. The new No. 1 signifies a rarity for Combs. As Dan Alley, Sam Banks and Nick Walsh wrote “Be By You,” it marks just the third of his chart-toppers that he didn’t write. It joins Jameson Rodgers’ Combs-featuring “Cold Beer Calling My Name,” which led for a week in 2021, and his cover of Tracy Chapman’s “Fast Car,” which spent five weeks in pole position in 2023. Meanwhile, Combs has a writing credit on 19 of the 22 songs on The Way I Am . Having noted that “Be By You” made its way to him through a friend, he shared in a statement in March that “the vibe and the melody immediately struck me.” Combs is one of just 11 artists in Country Airplay history, dating to the chart’s 1990 start, with at least 21 No. 1s, as he ties Thomas Rhett and Keith Urban’s totals. Kenny Chesney leads with 33, followed by Blake Shelton (30), Tim McGraw (29), Jason Aldean (27), Luke Bryan, Alan Jackson, George Strait (26 each) and Morgan Wallen (22). “Be By You” entered the multimetric Hot Country Songs chart at its No. 2 high in February and has spent its first six months in the top 10. It drew 7.3 million official streams and 34.3 million airplay audience impressions and sold 1,000 Aug. 7-13. It’s one of Combs’ 27 career top 10s on the chart, a sum that includes six No. 1s. Combs’ chart history also encompasses a Country Airplay No. 1 that he cowrote but didn’t record: Carly Pearce and Lee Brice’s “I Hope You’re Happy Now” led for a week in June 2020. All charts dated Aug. 29 will update on Billboard.com Tuesday, Aug. 25.

articles.title: The Dance Floor Isn’t Dead: Can Dance Music’s New Mainstream Surge in the U.S. Last?
articles.summary: The genre is growing faster than the wider industry, bringing renewed attention to the scene.
articles._body: It’s 2026, and dance music is back in the mainstream. Many ravers might find the concept of dance’s “return” misguided, given the genre’s mass appeal within the confines of its own ecosystem. From clubs to festivals to arena and stadium shows, every weekend fans are out filling venues. But with Luminate’s 2026 midyear report in June finding that dance/ electronic outgrew any other genre in the first half of 2026, the wider industry is now banging at the doors of the club. Related How Slayyyter, RAYE & Kehlani Won New Fans in 2026 — And Scored Their Biggest Tours to Date HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery BE:FIRST Is Ready for the World: Inside the J-Pop Superstars' Long-Planned U.S. Breakthrough One of the report’s key findings is that U.S. on-demand dance/electronic audio streams grew 18.9% year over year. This number is largely driven by a few key album releases: John Summit ’s CTRL Escape (in April), Illenium ’s Odyssey (February) and Slayyyter ’s Wor$t Girl in America (March), which also contained the highly streamed single “DANCE…” The most streamed dance track year to date is the Tinashe and Disco Lines smash “No Broke Boys,” which was also a rare Billboard Hot 100 crossover upon its release in 2025. Together, the three projects generated 416,900 equivalent album units through Aug. 13, according to Luminate, ranking at Nos. 1, 5 and 6, respectively, among the biggest dance albums so far this year. Last year at this time, only two of the top 10 highest-streaming dance albums had been released within the calendar year: FKA twigs ’ Eusexua at No. 7 and Skrillex ’ s F–k U Skrillex You Think Ur Andy Warhol but Ur Not!! <3 at No. 10. Related How Illenium’s Long History in Las Vegas Paved the Way for His Sphere Residency Meanwhile, the July 3 release of  Madonna ’s nightlife bacchanal Confessions II added 324.7 million official on-demand streams in the United States, helping dance/electronic at large generate 37.6 million equivalent album units from Jan. 2 through Aug. 6, up from the 28.8 million units over the same period last year and reflecting a 30.6% jump from the year before. Overall, dance music now constitutes 4.23% of the total U.S. industry through Aug. 6, up from 4.12% in 2025. This growth is also a reflection of a global dance scene that has matured into one that’s been shaping culture and fostering crossover artists for years — a trend dance industry experts say will only continue. “This isn’t just a top-down trend driven by a single radio hit; it’s happening from the ground up across hyper-specific, highly active scenes,” says SoundCloud senior director of music intelligence Wyatt Marshall . The streaming platform is a longtime incubator for many styles of dance — “dance/electronic” is itself an umbrella term for 100-plus subgenres — with countless online and IRL micro-scenes forging the sounds that ultimately cross over. Illenium, for example, is a product of the bass and future bass scenes that have heavy presences on SoundCloud and in the greater Denver area. John Summit comes from house and tech house, a white-hot genre in Miami, New York and Los Angeles that’s been forged at dance clubs and festivals. And longtime cult favorite Slayyyter went viral this year by incorporating elements of 2010s electro and blog house. Those artists’ catalogs have seen huge jumps year over year, too, boosted by their new projects: Illenium’s catalog is up 55%; Summit’s is up 94%; and Slayyyter’s has jumped 982%; even Madonna’s catalog has ballooned, up 134% year over year in terms of album consumption units. The fingerprints of dance have long been on music from major pop acts, from Coldplay to Britney Spears . More recently, BLACKPINK ’S 2025 comeback single “Jump” was produced by Diplo , who worked in elements of techno, drill, hardstyle, Eurodance and trance. There’s a direct line from Charli xcx ’s Brat to the hyperpop genre she helped pioneer, and Lady Gaga turned to French producer Gesaffelstein to bring hard edges to 2025’s Mayhem , which topped the Billboard 200 and has racked up 2.2 million equivalent album units in the U.S. through Aug. 13, according to Luminate. As dance gains visibility by feeding pop, its growth is also a function of it being particularly well-suited to a world where music discovery happens through phones. “The genre perfectly ticks all the boxes of modern music consumption: streaming, social media, live and festival culture, global sounds, a low barrier to entry, and a massive cultural moment,” says Marie Clausen , managing director of Ninja Tune, North America. “Short tracks and steady beats are ideal for algorithmic discovery, with high replay rates and low skip rates.” Clausen adds that the genre also performs exceptionally well on social media, “driving instant emotional reactions that lead to high replay, virality and global hits.” And, as it now goes, social fame paired with music that resonates can equate to actual fame. “More than ever, there are electronic artists who’ve been amplified into the mainstream and occupy musical levels historically reserved for media superstars,” says Stephen Satterthwaite , managing partner at Red Light Management. “When such acts can blow out stadiums or multi-night arenas and headline main stages at mainstream festivals, naturally, growth happens.” Related How Rüfüs Du Sol Achieved the Highest-Grossing Electronic Tour of All Time In terms of this rising-tide-lifts-all-boats mentality, Rüfüs Du Sol is on the final leg of the highest-grossing electronic tour of all time (including five sold-out dates at the Kia Forum in Englewood, Calif., in August), having already grossed $64 million from 727,000 tickets sold before this year even started, according to Billboard Boxscore; John Summit just headlined Lollapalooza and announced a show at

articles.title: 3 best Joey Porter Jr. trade destinations if Steelers decide on nuclear option
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are gearing up for an all or nothing 2026 season. Aaron Rodgers plans to retire after the season and will want to make the most of his last dance in the NFL. Naturally, that should lead the Steelers to want to surround Rodgers with as much talent as possible. But in a [
articles._body: The Pittsburgh Steelers are gearing up for an all or nothing 2026 season. Aaron Rodgers plans to retire after the season and will want to make the most of his last dance in the NFL. Naturally, that should lead the Steelers to want to surround Rodgers with as much talent as possible. But in a shocking twist, one Steelers defender could soon be on the move. NFL insider Jordan Schultz broke the news that multiple NFL teams view Porter Jr. as a potential trade target . “Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. is a name multiple teams around the NFL have wondered about as a potential trade target, per sources,” Schultz reported on Friday. “JPJ is in the final year of his rookie contract, and with where the CB market is, teams have wondered if Pittsburgh could ultimately be open to a move with the Pro Bowl caliber corner.” Reading between the lines, it seems like Porter Jr. does not want to play in 2026 without a new contract. He is on the final year of his rookie contract and should want to get in on the booming cornerback market. Remember, Seahawks CB Devon Witherspoon got a four-year, $132 million contract on August 15th. Witherspoon reset the market , establishing a $33 million per year threshold at the top. Porter Jr., as well as Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez, will want to top that figure when they get paid. Could this contract situation be enough to convince Pittsburgh to trade Porter Jr.? And if so, which teams might want to take him on? Three teams stand out as excellent trade destinations for Porter if the Steelers decide to deal him. Could Joey Porter Jr. be the final defensive piece for the Cowboys? Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Cowboys entered the offseason determined to rebuild their defense, and that’s exactly what they’ve done. Dallas hired a new defensive coordinator, traded up for Caleb Downs, and added multiple pieces on the defensive side of the ball. Jerry Jones recently admitted that he would make additional moves to improve the Cowboys roster . Perhaps that could lead Dallas to pursue a big trade for Porter Jr. There is no question that Porter Jr. would be an upgrade over Cobie Durant and DaRon Bland on the outside. Adding an elite cornerback like Porter Jr. would immediately give Dallas a strong CB1 and incredible depth at the position. Dallas, unlike other teams on this list, are a fearless organization that could attempt a big trade before the regular season. But the limiting factor for the Cowboys could be their tight salary cap in future seasons. They are already in the red for the 2027 season, so it is hard to imagine them being able to afford another big-money contract. Still, don’t count the Cowboys out of the Porter Jr. sweepstakes if he truly becomes available. The Lions could use a cornerback like Joey Porter Jr. more than anyone else Detroit needs to add talent at cornerback more than perhaps any other team in the NFL. The Lions desperately want to win the Super Bowl but they do not possess a perfect roster for the job. At least on the defensive side of the ball. Both of Detroit’s top safeties, Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph, are injured and may not be available to start the season. On top of that, the Lions cut Terrion Arnold following his recent legal troubles. Simply put, the Lions are absolutely starving for talent in their secondary. Could that lead them to acquire a player like Porter Jr.? On one hand, Detroit is the perfect team to pick up Porter Jr. as a one-year rental. If Porter Jr. is content to play on a contender, he could increase his stock before entering free agency in the spring. In that scenario, both sides could come out on top of in a trade. However, the contractual angle makes this more difficult. Would Porter Jr. be happy with a trade that does not immediately result in a new contract? After all, that appears to be his issue with Pittsburgh in the first place. Cost is another big barrier. The Steelers may ask for a premium draft pick, maybe even a first-round pick, in exchange for Porter Jr. There’s no denying that Porter Jr. and the Lions would be an excellent match. Unfortunately, it seems extremely unlikely that Detroit would jeopardize their future to go all in on any player, even one who could immediately elevate their defense. Would Joey Porter Jr. be attractive to a rebuilding team like the Dolphins? Amber Searls-Imagn Images It is only nature to zoom in on contending teams in trade situations like this. But that doesn’t mean a rebuilding team couldn’t get involved. The Dolphins have needs all over the roster, so of course a starting cornerback would be an excellent addition. Miami is the beginning stages of a rebuild under Jeff Hafley, a former defensive coordinator. He could easily prioritize building Miami’s defense before finishing the offense. That could make a player like Porter Jr. quite appealing to Miami’s coaching staff. The Dolphins already invested a first-round pick in Chris Johnson , But he projects to play mostly in the slot while also being cross trained to play on the boundary. If the Dolphins did add Porter Jr., he would immediately become their CB1 on the outside. And give themselves an excellent pair of cornerbacks to build around. Just like with Detroit, the price could be tricky. Miami doesn’t have any extra draft picks like this past offseason. The Dolphins probably don’t want to move their 2027 first-round pick, instead giving themselves a chance at a franchise quarterback. That being the case, they may not be able to offer enough to pry Porter Jr. away from PIttsburgh in the first place. Perhaps the Dolphins could dip into their future picks to put together a trade package for Porter Jr. The post 3 best Joey Porter Jr. trade destinations if Steelers decide on nuclear option appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Don Kelly gets 100% real on Paul Skenes’ velocity decline
articles.summary: The story surrounding the Pittsburgh Pirates over the past few weeks has been Paul Skenes’ play, and most notably, the drop in his production. There has been nothing but optimism surrounding one of the best pitchers in the league, and manager Don Kelly recently shared how the team is managi
articles._body: The story surrounding the Pittsburgh Pirates over the past few weeks has been Paul Skenes’ play , and most notably, the drop in his production. There has been nothing but optimism surrounding one of the best pitchers in the league, and manager Don Kelly recently shared how the team is managing his velocity decline. “The other day we were looking at 80 or 85 pitches coming off of 65. We’ll see how he recovers and how he’s doing, but he felt a lot better on Wednesday,” Kelly said on MLB Network Radio. Kelly was then asked if there were any concerns with his velocity. “I think that the velo this year has been down and even consistently from the beginning of the season. I think that it’s something that you always have to be mindful of and monitor, and I think that the main thing is that Paul says that he feels good,” Kelly said. "The main thing is that Paul (Skenes) says he's good." #Pirates https://t.co/fGPbvbj8w4 pic.twitter.com/reLsc7GbYS — MLB Network Radio on SiriusXM (@MLBNetworkRadio) August 21, 2026 The good thing is that the team doesn’t seem to be panicking; they’re hoping that Skenes can get back to being the player that everyone knows. As of now, the Pirates will have an uphill battle in trying to get into the postseason, as they’re currently 63-66 and are in fourth place in the NL Central. If they want to go on a run down this stretch, Skenes playing better will have to be the key, and the rest of the clubhouse will have to step up as well. It’ll be interesting to see how things pan out for the Pirates as the season continues. The post Don Kelly gets 100% real on Paul Skenes’ velocity decline appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Former Heat guard Max Strus shares honest admission on playing with Jimmy Butler
articles.summary: LA Clippers guard Max Strus opened up about his experience with Jimmy Butler during their time with the Miami Heat. For many, the Heat’s Giannis Antetokounmpo trade marks a new era after the Butler years, following his 2025 trade to the Golden State Warriors. Jimmy led the Heat to two Final
articles._body: LA Clippers guard Max Strus opened up about his experience with Jimmy Butler during their time with the Miami Heat. For many, the Heat’s Giannis Antetokounmpo trade marks a new era after the Butler years, following his 2025 trade to the Golden State Warriors . Jimmy led the Heat to two Finals appearances , where he shone despite his team coming up short 4-1 to the Denver Nuggets. Strus says Butler is unlike any other teammate he’s ever had, taking in the good with the bad, as he explained, per Barstool Sports’ Pardon My Take. “I don’t think there’s anything else like him,” Strus said. “From what I experienced and what I saw during that time, I’ve never seen anything like that in my life.” Max Strus says Jimmy Butler’s focus on the court for the Heat was not only what made him unique, but also his demeanor off of it. “Oh, he’ll drink a beer in the hot tub after,” Strus added. “He’s just the most normal dude. He’s an a****** for sure. He’ll go and drink wine after the game. Drink a couple of beers and do it again the next day. He can get away from it so easily. Then when he has to turn it on, he can just flip a switch in the fourth quarter.” When asked if Butler’s approach is an acquired taste, Struss says that’s one way to put it. “It’s kind of like that,” Strus replied. “But he’s also like an a****** towards you. One day, you’ll look at him, and he won’t even acknowledge you. You can like go to dinner with him the night before, like you’re his best friend. Then, the next morning, you go to practice, and he won’t even look at you or say hi to you. And you’re like, ‘Damn, what did I do at dinner last night?’ “Then the game starts, and he’s your best friend again. You got to play the card like, yeah, Jimmy’s gonna be Jimmy. I just got to a point where I didn’t give a f*** anymore.” Max Strus talking about what it’s like to be a teammate with Jimmy Butler including their secret handshake where they just dap and flip eachother off pic.twitter.com/wTtrtsCMAA — Barstool Sports (@barstoolsports) August 21, 2026 For Strus, the approach of not taking Butler’s demeanor personally helped him understand his teammate and led to a handshake that ended with both flipping each other off as a fitting conclusion to their signature handshake. The post Former Heat guard Max Strus shares honest admission on playing with Jimmy Butler appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles._body: Joe and Donell Jones faced off in a Verzuz battle of ’90s R&B royalty on Thursday (Aug. 20). Joe raised the stakes when responding to Jones reuniting 702 for “Get It Together” earlier in the night by having 50 Cent and G-Unit’s Tony Yayo and Uncle Murda join him on stage for round 14. With the R&B-favoring crowd in a frenzy, 50 took it back to the G-Unit days with a performance of the group’s Marvin Gaye-sampling Joe collaboration “Wanna Get to Know You,” which landed on the Unit’s 2003 Beg for Mercy debut and peaked at No. 15 on the Billboard Hot 100. 50 stuck around to perform the Power theme song “Big Rich Town” to ensure another round victory for Joe against the “Where I Wanna Be” singer. Fans seemed to appreciate 50 popping out, while others on social media called him out for dodging a Verzuz battle with T.I. earlier this year. Joe’s preparation paid off, as he was a technician on the Verzuz stage, from his performance to song selection, which kept him steps ahead of Donell Jones. Fans agreed and he dominated the Verzuz scorecard with an 18-2 victory. Joe leaned on high-profile collaborations such as his Mariah Carey team-up “Thank God I Found You” — but pulled out the Nas remix — as well as the Mystikal-assisted “Stutter,” both of which topped the Hot 100. “For me, it’s not really a Verzuz — it’s a celebration,” Donell Jones told Complex before the battle. “We’re not going to do what the other guys did where it’s beefing back and forth. We’re grown-ass men. We both have two great catalogs. We’re going to treat it as such.” Watch G-Unit’s performance with Joe below. View this post on Instagram

articles.title: Nvidia just showed that the harness, not the AI model, is now the real hero
articles.summary: Nvidia research shows that AI agents can perform well, and not go off the deep end, through fine-tuning, even if the AI model isn't that great at the task.
articles._body: Nvidia published some interesting new research on Friday suggesting it’s the harness, more than the underlying model, that is far more important when asking an AI to do long-horizon tasks. A harness is the software wrapper around an AI model — the tools, memory management, and rules that turn a raw model into something that can act on its own. The TL;DR: Simply by using a custom harness tweaked to handle memory well and including a “supervisor” boss-like component, researchers got Claude Opus 5 to achieve a 100% score on the interactive reasoning benchmark ARC-AGI-3 — a set of 2D games with no instructions, where the model has to figure out how to play and win, similar to how a human would. (That’s a benchmark that has particularly irked rival frontier lab OpenAI.) Without the harness, Opus 5 scored 30%, which was the top result among all the models tested. Nvidia’s research is another indicator that, while model choice does matter, the model itself — the part that acts as the agent’s “brain” — is a smaller part of an agentic system than many AI users realize, especially for long-horizon tasks. The harness is what makes a model an agent: It handles memory, context, and feedback. “Generally speaking, the world interprets an agent almost as an API of the model,” Adel El Hallak, vice president of product in Nvidia’s AI unit (pictured above), tells TechCrunch. But an agent is actually more than that. “It is the model. It is the scaffolding around the model, which we call the harness, i.e. the set of tools that it utilizes. It is the runtime and the associated skills and libraries that we give it access to.” Long-horizon tasks are those that require stringing many decisions together, sometimes over days, to produce completed work. This is in contrast to an AI just spitting out a response to a prompt. Figuring out how to get an AI to do long-horizon tasks without getting distracted and going off in la-la land is one of the holy grails in agentic research. For example: Microsoft published research in April that tested 19 LLMs on long-horizon tasks involving document editing and discovered that all the models, including frontier ones, filled the documents with errors. (If humans produced work like that, they would be promptly fired.) Models stringing decisions together on their own have also been caught deleting their users’ files or even whole databases or turning to criminal behavior, from collusion to hacking, to achieve their objectives. The choice by Nvidia researchers to use this interactive reasoning benchmark for their tests is particularly meaningful, almost funny. A 100% score means that the model can beat the games as well as humans. OpenAI was so flustered by its models’ abysmal scores (less than 10%) on ARC-AGI-3 that it conducted its own research last month. Like Nvidia, OpenAI discovered that simply by tweaking two settings on the harness, its models tripled their scores. But none of the models came close to hitting a 100% score, like Nvidia’s researchers achieved. They showed that the harness needs a “supervisor” component that prods the agent in the right direction if it gets stuck. “The more interesting part was introducing a supervising agent in addition to your main agent that’s doing the work,” El Hallak said. It “almost acts like a CEO to nudge the agent when it goes off direction or starts exploring a path that it might lead to a dead end, or re-explore a path that it had previously trod.” While the concept of the supervising agent isn’t exactly new, today most agent users are relying on only one layer for their harness, like Claude Code, Codex, or Hermes. Nvidia researchers created their own souped-up harness called the Agentic Variation Operators (AVO). Note that this isn’t a new Nvidia product. Nvidia instead produces lots of open bits and pieces of tech for building harnesses under the Nemo brand. Some of that tech is commercial, while much is openly available. Still, Nvidia’s results add to the growing evidence that model choice is far from the only factor in agentic performance. In July, for instance, Databricks published some stunning research that shows that the harness, more than the model, dramatically impacts AI costs. “You can pick the same model but different harnesses, and you get significantly more cost if you use the wrong harness,” Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi told TechCrunch. “So you think, oh, this is an expensive model. This is a cheap model. But wait, which harness are you using? That itself can 2x your cost.” Nvidia’s larger point is to show that open harnesses, like open models, put users in control far more than they realize. “We believe, and we’re demonstrating with the ecosystem, how open harnesses allow you to turn a lot more knobs to drive up that accuracy,” El Hallak said. “It relates to OpenAI slowing down the training of their models,” as a result of models creating security breaches. “We believe in having an open agent stack — where you have control across the harness, across the infrastructure, across the runtime — is what’s required for us to usher the ecosystem forward and securely,” he added.

articles._body: Nick Saban and Mario Cristobal apparently remain locked in a friendly conference debate. On The Pat McAfee Show on Friday, Saban joked that the Miami head coach regularly calls him with “this ACC bullsh—” while trying to argue that the ACC is better than the SEC. The legendary former Alabama coach is not buying it. "I love Mario Cristobal and he's great recruiter.. He calls me about the ACC all the time" Coach Saban #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/Vjh8HVMn8D — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) August 21, 2026 “He calls me up with this ACC bullshit,” Saban said while shaking his head. “He’s always trying to convince me the ACC is better than the SEC. The SEC has nine teams in the Top 25. That is all I know. It’s a deep conference; it just is.” “It is what it is. He is never going to convince me that the ACC is better than the SEC.” Saban won six national championships at Alabama and another at LSU, building his legacy in the SEC. He experienced the conference’s demanding schedule and enormous expectations firsthand. Cristobal has a compelling response after leading Miami to the national championship game last season . The Hurricanes’ run gave the ACC valuable credibility and proved that its best teams can compete on college football’s biggest stage. Still, one successful season will not persuade Saban to abandon his SEC loyalty. The exchange also highlights the relationship between the two coaches. Cristobal worked under Saban at Alabama from 2013 through 2016 as his offensive line coach, giving them enough familiarity to argue about their respective conferences without the conversation becoming overly serious. Until the ACC consistently matches the SEC’s depth and postseason success, those phone calls are unlikely to change his mind. articles.title: NBA 2K27 MyCAREER Features Eras & Co-Op Mode
articles.summary: MyCAREER obviously returns to NBA 2K27 this year, bringing a new NBA journey for players to experience. For those new to the series, MyCAREER is a player-career mode that’s more than just playing games. But this year, the developers heavily expanded on the concept by adding Eras as well as
articles._body: MyCAREER obviously returns to NBA 2K27 this year, bringing a new NBA journey for players to experience. For those new to the series, MyCAREER is a player-career mode that’s more than just playing games. But this year, the developers heavily expanded on the concept by adding Eras as well as a Co-Op mode. Without further ado, let’s dive right in. NBA 2K27 MyCAREER – Everything You Need to Know Overall the three biggest new things coming to NBA 2K27 MyCAREER this year is: MyCAREER Eras A Brand New Narrative (Fire & Concrete) Co-Op MyCAREER For the first time ever in NBA 2K history, you can start a MyCAREER in one of five historical Eras : The Magic vs. Bird Era (1984) The Jordan Era (1991) The Kobe Era (2003) The LeBro Era (2010) The Steph Era (2016) Originally, these Eras and their teams weren’t available in MyCAREER in this capacity. But now, you have a chance to insert your MyPLAYER into these Eras and play a completely different type of career. Each era features not only different rosters, but rules, presentation elements, league structure, and more. When you play in one of the historical eras, everything remains locked to historical accuracy. You could start the Jordan Era in 1991 and play long enough to see the titular athlete play in Washington in 2001. Nothing will be different and you’ll experience history as you try to rewrite it. In terms of presentation, each Era features specific locker rooms, HUDs, score bugs, stat overlays, and on-screen filters. Additionally, any Era you pick will be built around Eras Moments. Essentially, these are objectives you can complete as you advance through a 40-level reward track. Fire & Concrete Of course, MyCAREER still features a modern day story, called “Fire & Concrete” this year. This cinematic story is 11 chapters long and, according to the developers, over twice the length of NBA 2K26’s story. Overall, it follows your journey from High School to the G League and into the NBA. In terms of the story, it begins with you being a top prospect who’s already committed to Duke. However, a car accident sidelines those plans and you fast forward two years later where you find yourself in New York City. Show off your skills at the proving ground, Rucker Park, as your cousin Cam (Vince Staples) gets your back through it all. There’s plenty of characters you’ll meet in your MyCAREER journey, as well as key moments like the NBA Draft and important games during your season. This year your draft position is not fixed, and how you perform before your NBA journey impacts where you land on the draft board. Play hard and earn the #1 overall selection, or if you want, you can completely skip the prelude and select the team you want to play for instead. Key Games appear in your second, and there are eight brand-new Key Game sets in 2K27. Each set takes place over the course of half a season (roughly), giving you objectives and goals to meet during the year. Co-Op Comes to MyCAREER in NBA 2K27 Lastly and perhaps most importantly, Co-Op comes to MyCAREER. In your MyCAREER story, you’ll meet a character named Trace Miller, who you meet in the G League. Miller is in the same position as you, working hard to earn that job in the starting lineup of an NBA team. He’s also who your teammate will control thanks to Co-Op. After you first meet Trace, you’ll be able to choose one of nine build templates for him to use: Giannis Antetokounmpo Cade Cunningham Stephen Curry Luka Dončić Kevin Durant Anthony Edwards Donovan Mitchell Nikola Jokić Kawhi Leonard Trace’s build determines his physicals, but you can earn points throughout the experience to improve his attributes, Badges, and playstyle. After he joins your squad, you can invite a friend into your MyCAREER, and they will control Trace. Co-Op in NBA 2K27 MyCAREER is extremely flexible. You can activate it or skip on a game-to-game basis. But if you really want, you can experience the entire MyCAREER story together, including cutscenes. When your teammate isn’t on, Trace is controlled by the AI. Even if you don’t want to play Co-Op, Trace will still be there to back you up. So think of him as a secondary character your journey to greatness. Overall, that includes all the major details about NBA 2K27 MyCAREER . We can’t wait to try out Co-Op MyCAREER, as well as the MyCAREER eras. Furthermore, we look forward to seeing the narrative of Fire and Concrete. Lastly, for more gaming and NBA news, visit ClutchPoints. Furthermore, subscribe to our newsletter for more weekly info. articles.title: Hornets get roasted by fans after framing NBA Play-In Tournament net
articles.summary: Success can be relative in the NBA. Despite failing to make the playoffs, the Charlotte Hornets had plenty to celebrate last season. They surpassed their win total from the previous two campaigns combined and delivered the Spectrum Center a rousing NBA Play-In Tournament victory over the Miami He
articles._body: Success can be relative in the NBA. Despite failing to make the playoffs, the Charlotte Hornets had plenty to celebrate last season. They surpassed their win total from the previous two campaigns combined and delivered the Spectrum Center a rousing NBA Play-In Tournament victory over the Miami Heat. The franchise took a sizable step forward, and although fans have mixed feelings about the LaMelo Ball trade , there is still optimism pulsing through the streets of the Queen City. But how does one acknowledge progress without becoming a punchline? The Hornets may not be the right organization to ask. Charlotte could not resist commemorating its best accomplishment since 2016, and in doing so, it reminded people of its bleak history. The Hornets’ X account dropped a clip from an episode of Reel Access, a video documentary series that gives fans a behind-the-scenes look at the team, and this one was a doozy. While spotlighting Coby White, who re-signed on a three-year, 74 million contract in free agency, the squad unveiled a framed picture of the Play-In net from its 127-126 triumph versus Miami. Charlotte got thumped by the Orlando Magic in its second Play-In contest and have yet to win a postseason series since reentering the NBA as the Bobcats in 2004. It is easy to see how this gesture would go over with the public. offseason & more. our most exclusive behind the scenes series – episode 1 of reel access, out now on YouTube! pic.twitter.com/rVnS70Dv9e — Charlotte Hornets (@hornets) August 20, 2026 “The net from our last play in game? holy this franchise is poverty,” @demonhourslol opined on X . “Omg… That might be the saddest s**t I’ve ever seen a team do…” @CeeJayJohnson91 commented . “Remember when the Lakers put up an In-Season tournament championship banner? This just took Jeanie Buss off the hook… HOLY…” LaMelo Ball, who drew the ire of fans in South Beach and throughout the country after he contributed to Bam Adebayo’s game-ending back injury , made the decisive basket with less than five seconds remaining in overtime. Now that he is on the Minnesota Timberwolves, it might be a little awkward to memorialize a win that is most remembered for his heroic drive. One sports fan certainly feels that way. “The framed play-in net is so depressing LMFAOOOO and then decided to trade away the whole reason that play-in net is even in their possession, what an embarrassment of a franchise,” @halibuckets remarked . Ball obviously played a big role in the Hornets’ rise, but he also shot 2-of-16 from 3-point range in that first NBA Play-In Tournament clash. Midseason acquisition Coby White was far more efficient from the field and also drilled the trey that forced OT against the Heat . He deserves fair recognition. Framing the net is a questionable call, however. After trading away Ball and Miles Bridges this offseason, Charlotte has put itself directly under the microscope. If the team backslides in 2026, then this polarizing Play-In net decision will be used to highlight the Hornets’ longstanding status as one of America’s least respected franchises. The post Hornets get roasted by fans after framing NBA Play-In Tournament net appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Motorola's GrapheneOS phones will launch in 2027 priced higher than Pixels
articles.summary: The private Android-based OS will expand beyond Pixels next year.
articles._body: Several months ago, Motorola and the makers of GrapheneOS announced a team-up that would expand support for the privacy-centric OS to beyond Google's Pixel phones. The announcement, however, was bereft of details. Now, the creators of the OS have taken to Mastodon (naturally) to provide an update . Moto's GrapheneOS phones are on track to launch in 2027, but they'll cost a pretty penny. The upcoming Moto devices won't ship with GrapheneOS, but they will be fully supported by the project with help from Moto itself. So far, only Pixel phones have met GrapheneOS's strict hardware requirements to ensure the highest level of security and privacy. The software, which is based on Android, includes features like enhanced memory protection, granular network permissions, customizable app sandboxing, and a duress code that can be used to wipe your phone. (That last one got an activist charged with a felony earlier this year after he used it to delete his data during a customs interrogation.) According to the GrapheneOS team, the upcoming Moto phones will be premium flagship devices. The team expects pricing to be even higher than Pixel phones, which is saying something. The current Pixel lineup starts at $900 for the base model Pixel 11, a $100 increase from last year. The Pixel 11 Pro XL price has gone up to a whopping $1,300 this year. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Klay Thompson to sign with Heat after Mavericks buyout agreement
articles.summary: Klay Thompson and the Dallas Mavericks have officially reached a buyout agreement, the team announced on Friday afternoon. Upon clearing waivers, league sources told ClutchPoints that Thompson intends to sign a contract with the Miami Heat. Throughout the offseason, the Mavs had pushed back at th
articles._body: Klay Thompson and the Dallas Mavericks have officially reached a buyout agreement , the team announced on Friday afternoon. Upon clearing waivers, league sources told ClutchPoints that Thompson intends to sign a contract with the Miami Heat. Throughout the offseason, the Mavs had pushed back at the idea of buying Thompson out of his contract, making it clear to rival teams that they intended to trade the five-time All-Star. The Heat have long held interest in Thompson, but only by way of a buyout, where they would then be able to offer him their remaining $8.9 million mid-level exception. Although the Mavericks did not hold any interest in buying Thompson out, prefering to trade him and receive some type of value in return, the organization ultimately decided to respect the veteran’s wishes upon him approaching the team’s management and formally asking for a buyout in recent days, sources said. After two years in Dallas, Thompson is now prepared to head to South Beach and team up with All-Stars Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo in hopes of adding another championship ring to his collection. “Klay is one of the great players and competitors of his generation, and we are grateful for everything he brought to the Mavericks organization,” Mavericks President of Basketball Operations Masai Ujiri said in the team’s press release regarding Klay’s buyout. “We have tremendous respect for Klay and all that he has accomplished throughout his career, and we wish him nothing but the best moving forward.” In 141 games with the Mavericks after joining them by way of a sign-and-trade from the Golden State Warriors in 2024, Thompson averaged 12.9 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 1.7 assists per game while shooting 40.3 percent from the floor and 38.7 percent from 3-point range. For his career, Thompson has shot 40.9 percent from 3-point range and ranks fourth on the NBA’s all-time threes leaderboard with 2,899 triples, trailing only Stephen Curry (4,248), James Harden (3,390), and Ray Allen (2,973). As a four-time NBA champion with the Warriors, Thompson brings years of title and playoff experience to a Heat team that expects to be in the Eastern Conference championship mix. He is also reunited with forward Andrew Wiggins, who was a key part of the Warriors’ 2022 championship run. After signing Tim Hardaway Jr. using part of their mid-level exception in free agency, the Heat made it clear that their top priority was pursuing LeBron James. Ultimately, James decided to join the Philadelphia 76ers, leaving Miami with a chunk of financial flexibility via its mid-level exception. Thompson instantly became the organization’s top target, which is why they did not make an offer using their MLE to Bradley Beal or DeMar DeRozan, two other veteran free agents linked to Miami. The Heat have about $10.6 million to work with before reaching their first-apron hard cap. With the Heat, Thompson is expected to hold a role similar to what Ray Allen held during the end of his career during the 2012-13 and 2013-14 seasons in Miami. Allen will forever be remembered in Heat lore with his infamous game-tying three-point shot against the San Antonio Spurs in Game 6 of the 2013 NBA Finals. The Heat would go on to win Game 6 in overtime thanks to Allen, and they went on to win Game 7 to capture their second straight championship. Like Allen, who was 37 when signing with the Heat, Thompson is 36 and at peace with the idea of being an elite 3-point weapon as a catch-and-shoot option for his team, especially if they are in the title mix. Throughout the offseason, Thompson and the Mavericks were on the same page about moving on. Thompson wanted to join a contending team, and he made this clear recently with comments regarding his situation in Dallas. “I want to compete for a championship. Not necessarily win another one, but have the chance to go and try and get another one,” Thompson said on a Twitch live stream recently. “I want to play a role on a team that can make a deep playoff run, whether it’s this season or next season. That’s really my only goal.” Once this buyout with Dallas is official, Thompson can officially ink a new deal to join the Heat, marking the first time in his career he will play in the Eastern Conference. articles.title: 49ers’ Brock Purdy further explains desire to run more this season
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers will be leaning on Brock Purdy to elevate their offense this season, and he’s shown that he can do so. This season, he plans on taking things a bit further, as he wants to use his legs more to maximize the offense. Purdy was recently on the Pat McAfee Show and [̷
articles._body: The San Francisco 49ers will be leaning on Brock Purdy to elevate their offense this season, and he’s shown that he can do so. This season, he plans on taking things a bit further, as he wants to use his legs more to maximize the offense. Purdy was recently on the Pat McAfee Show and shared his desire for wanting to create opportunities with his legs more. “I don’t know if I’ll be a Lamar Jackson out there by any means, but there’s always times on film where it’s like, I probably could use my feet there to pick up that 1st down and whatnot. But I think that’s always within my training to make sure that I’m in shape and I am athletic enough to get out of the pocket, make plays off the scramble and whatnot,” Purdy said. "There's always times on film where I probably could have used my feet a little bit more.. I've gotta be able to make plays off the scramble" @brockpurdy13 #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/jaYISThi2S — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) August 21, 2026 The 49ers’ quarterback had mentioned wanting to use his legs more the day before in an interview with ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. “I’m never going to be a 4.4 guy, 4.5 guy,” Purdy said. “The thing I pride myself on is moving quickly, moving the chains when I need 10, 12 yards. I think I can add that for our offense, for sure. Not looking for that kind of stuff, but being able to fall back when those moments happen, like, ‘alright dude, I have the legs to do this, the mobility to do this, the athleticism.’…As I get older, I want to maintain that.” Even if he doesn’t have the speed like most mobile quarterbacks in the league, it could still be a huge opportunity for him to create plays for the offense when they’re on the field. His legs could be the difference between the team picking up a 3rd-and-short or running it in at the goal line for a touchdown. articles._body: The release of NBA 2K27 is just around the corner, and that means everyone from casual gamers to NBA players will be locked into the new game trying to come out on top. Oklahoma City Thunder star Chet Holmgren grew up a gamer, and like most players, is looking to see what he’s like in NBA 2K27. This year’s version of NBA 2K27 features a brand new mode, pulling from the MyNBA Eras. Gamers will be able to bring their MyPlayer and start the MyCareer in five different eras : — The Magic vs. Bird Era (1984) — The Jordan Era (1991) — The Kobe Era (2003) — The LeBron Era (2010) — The Steph Era (2016) Each era will feature historically-locked rosters, trades, and player movement to keep the league behaving exactly as it unfolded, allowing players to be an active participant in NBA history. In addition to all that, each era will feature historic achievements and objectives to progress while also featuring era-specific settings like locker rooms, arenas, score-bugs, and more. With the new era-specific additions to NBA 2K27, ClutchPoints had a chance to chat with Oklahoma City Thunder star Chet Holmgren to gauge his thoughts on the new mode. The first question posed to Holmgren? “If you could go back and team up with any player in NBA history all-time, who would it be? Can you even pick just one?” “Ooh, that’s a tough one,” Holmgren responded. “Yeah, I don’t know. Can I maybe give a starting five? Obviously Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant. Then I’d say like OKC Kevin Durant, and one more… I’d say 2011 Dirk Nowitzki.” A starting five of Jordan, Bryant, Durant, Nowitzki, and Holmgren is solid, covering both the offensive and defensive sides of the basketball. Holmgren had a big year of the Thunder, averaging 17.1 points, 8.9 rebounds, 1.7 assists, and 1.9 blocks per game while shooting 55.7 percent from the field. The points, rebounds, and field goal percentage were all career highs for the third year big man out of Gonzaga. You can check out Chet Holmgren’s full interview with ClutchPoints at NBA 2K27 Community Day here . NBA 2K27 is set to release worldwide on September 4, 2026, with Early Access for the game beginning on Wednesday, August 26 for players who get the Deluxe Edition and Ultra Edition. articles._body: Matt Campbell understands the expectations waiting for him at Penn State. During a Friday appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, the Nittany Lions’ new head coach described seeing Beaver Stadium late at night with the lights shining over the venue’s ongoing expansion. "I look at the lights on every night in this stadium and it's so special.. This is one of the great places to play College Football" ~ @CoachMC_PSU #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/SdCw1a4tPh — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) August 21, 2026 “I would be remiss to say, man, at 10:30-11:00 at night and you look at this expansion and the lights on in the stadium. ‘Look at this place. Look how special it is to play in one of the great places to play college football.’ We are really fortunate to do it. I am excited for the opportunity, but I am more excited to give ur fanbase and this university a team that can represent the history of this place the right way.” Campbell called Penn State “one of the great places to play college football” and said he feels fortunate to lead the program. However, his most important message focused on building a team capable of representing the university’s proud history. That should immediately catch the attention of Penn State fans. Campbell enters his first season in Happy Valley with an opportunity to establish a new culture. He is not interested in ignoring the program’s past or starting over completely. Instead, he wants to build upon the foundation already in place. James Franklin did a respectable job of maintaining Penn State’s national relevance. The Nittany Lions consistently competed near the top of the Big Ten and remained involved in the College Football Playoff conversation. Campbell’s challenge is taking the next step. Representing Penn State’s history “the right way” cannot simply mean producing winning seasons. At a program with this much tradition, support, and access to resources, the ultimate standard must be competing for Big Ten and national championships every season. While Thompson could be headed to his third team before the 2026-27 season, he clapped back in the comments section of a post on Instagram. When a user compared Allen leading the Milwaukee Bucks to the Eastern Conference Finals in 2001 to Thompson’s secondary role on the Golden State Warriors, Thompson reminded the fan of his role before Kevin Durant joined the Warriors in the comments section of the Instagram post. “You do realize I was the 2nd leading scorer on two championship teams without KD? You want me to go to a bad team and put up empty stats, that’s easy buddy,” Thompson said. “Holy s***, I led the 2016 playoffs in points scored you casuals.” Klay Thompson got into it with some fans on Instagram his career got compared to Ray Allen’s “You do realize I was the 2nd leading scorer on two championship teams without KD? You want me to go to a bad team and put up empty stats, that’s easy buddy.” “Holy sh**, I led the… pic.twitter.com/oDPZG7BoFJ — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 21, 2026 Thompson averaged 21.7 points, two points shy of Stephen Curry’s team-leading 23.8 points, in the 2015 NBA Finals. Then, in the Warriors’ Finals rematch against the Cleveland Cavs, he was the second-leading scorer once again (19.6), trailing Curry by three points (22.6) in 2016. Ray Allen led the Bucks with 27.1 points, 5.4 assists, and 3.3 rebounds per game against Allen Iverson and the Philadelphia 76ers across seven games in the 2001 Eastern Conference Finals. Iverson and the 76ers eliminated the Bucks, 4-3, to advance to the NBA Finals. However, he did lead the Warriors in points (582) throughout Golden State’s playoff run, averaging 24.3 points per game to Curry’s 25.1. Klay Thompson’s fate ahead of 2026-27 remains undecided Mavericks veteran Klay Thompson says LeBron James was the toughest player he had to guard as he and the Warriors defeated James and the Cavs three times in four consecutive Finals meetings between 2015 and 2018. Thompson, 36, is reportedly hoping to compete for a fifth NBA title this upcoming season. Thompson has been reportedly linked to possibly joining Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Heat, according to NBA insider Marc Stein. “Miami continues to sit at the front of the line of teams hoping that Dallas buys out Klay Thompson,” Stein reported. “The Heat this week missed out on well-known target when Beal elected to re-sign with the Clippers. The Stein Line has learned that there has indeed been direct contact this offseason between new Mavericks president Masai Ujiri and Thompson, but Dallas has maintained since mid-June that it prefers to trade Thompson if possible rather than buy him out. “Two sources briefed on the process said this week that it remains unclear how the situation will play out. Dallas currently has 16 standard contracts on its books — one more than the league maximum that will be allowed as of Oct. 19 — but Thompson’s fate remained undecided as of Sunday.” Thompson and the Mavericks could reach a sign-and-trade between now and the start of the regular season. articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks plan to have a big season on offense, but they may be without one of their key receivers, and he might be sidelined for the year. Jake Bobo was carted off the field with a knee injury in their joint practice against the Tennessee Titans. The wide receiver went down after goin
articles._body: The Seattle Seahawks plan to have a big season on offense , but they may be without one of their key receivers, and he might be sidelined for the year. Jake Bobo was carted off the field with a knee injury in their joint practice against the Tennessee Titans. The wide receiver went down after going for a catch on the sideline and landed awkwardly. Head coach Mike Macdonald gave an update on Bobo’s injury the next day and noted that it was serious, according to Gregg Bell of the News Tribune. “Coach Mike Macdonald says it’s a major knee injury for WR Jake Bobo. Says heart goes out to a beloved Seahawks player. Both teams took a knee, said a prayer for Bobo,” Bell wrote on X, formerly Twitter. Bobo appeared in 11 games for the Seahawks last season but mostly played on special teams. In the postseason, he finished with two catches, 33 yards and a touchdown. It doesn’t seem like there is an official diagnosis on Bobo’s injury, but usually when the cart comes out for the player, it’s more bad news than good. If that’s the case, the Seahawks may be looking for someone to replace Bobo, or they might decide to look internally. It was hard seeing Bobo getting consistent playing time at receiver this season with Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed, so he probably would’ve seen most of his snaps on special teams. The Seahawks had one of the better offenses in the league last season, and that should be the case again this upcoming season. They did lose a big part of their offense, with Kenneth Walker III signing with the Kansas City Chiefs in the offseason. They’ll now lean on Zach Charbonnet to take control of the backfield, and he’s shown throughout his time with the team that he can do it.
